heading: Background
content: In academic and professional writing, documents usually start as rough drafts. These drafts may not follow any formatting rules initially. Writers focus on content first and apply styles later according to institutional or project guidelines.

heading: Introduction
content: This project aims to automate the process of validating uploaded documents and images inside academic reports or project submissions. The system will identify whether an image is relevant to the surrounding text content using semantic similarity models.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Students often include irrelevant images or diagrams in their project reports either intentionally or unintentionally. Evaluators must manually inspect each image to verify its relevance, which is time‑consuming. This project will automate this verification process using AI.

heading: Objectives
content: Primary objectives include: - Develop a semantic similarity model for image–text relevance checking. - Integrate the model with a Flutter frontend and Python backend. - Provide automated alerts for irrelevant images. - Improve document quality and evaluator efficiency.

heading: Methodology
content: The following technologies and methods will be used: - Random Forest model for baseline text classification - Image feature extraction using Python-based toolkit - Semantic similarity evaluation - Flutter for UI and Python for backend APIs

heading: Expected Outcomes
content: The system will accurately detect mismatched or irrelevant content and notify the user to upload a more appropriate image.

heading: Introduction
content: This project’s aim is to create a software called “Secure Backup and Encryption Software” which will protect the data by encrypting and backup processes. The user will have an option to choose files/folders to protect, that our software will encrypt using AES-256-GCM. It will automate backups according to schedule defined by user and keeps versions for duration specified by user (for example, 3-4 days) so that user should also have  an option to recover not just the most recent backup, but also the previous ones. This functionality provides protection against accidental data loss or changes.

heading: Abstract
content: Final Year Project (FYP) reports are frequently a very tedious and professional writing where students have to adhere to specific guidelines of the institutions. Formatting by hand takes up precious time, and distracts the actual research, and often the issue of inconsistencies ensues. The current project suggests creating an AI-driven Report Formatter that will automate the process of formatting the reports, making sure they are formatted in accordance with the institution-specific template and protecting the academic integrity. The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning to identify the elements of a document (headings, paragraphs, tables, figures and references) and uses these elements to apply formatting rules. An exclusive administration panel will enable the institutions to post and maintain their own templates to guarantee a high level of flexibility in the various universities. The innovations are AI-based with ethical vs. unethical image detection, which filters indecent or otherwise unacademic images, and a voice-activated formatting interface, which lets the user set formatting instructions by simply speaking to the computer and improving accessibility. Other functions provided are plagiarism and grammar check, absent section suggestions, and live preview. Word, PDF and LaTeX export options will be used to provide a high number of compatibility. The proposed solution alleviates the administrative workload of formatting, enhances academic integrity and increases accessibility in students by incorporating smart content classification and ethical protection as well as multi-modal interaction with users. In the end, the Report Formatter hopes to be a smart academic assistant that fills the gap between the creation of content and the presentation of the professional work, thus contributing to the high level of productivity and the quality of academic work in general.

heading: Background
content: Report writing is part and parcel of academic and professional work. In tertiary education, learners have to deliver reports, theses, and project documentation which has to be in perfect format according to the requirements that are given by their institutions of higher learning. Such formatting guidelines usually include font types, font size, headings hierarchy, margin requirements, table format, reference format and other organizational aspects. Although these standards are required to ensure uniformity and readability, the manual formatting is normally time consuming, difficult and cannot be done without errors. Students are often wasted in matching headings, numbering lists and the reference styles more than in the actual content of their work. The latter is even more difficult when the various institutions have varying formatting standards. As an example, one university might recommend using the APA style form of reference, and another one to use IEEE or Chicago style. Equally, the specifications on the appearance of the table, the position of the caption and the structure of the sections can be quite diverse. This is because the absence of a universal tool that can adapt to various formatting needs makes compliance quite challenging to the students, and in fact, unintentional non-compliance to institutional standards can be experienced. These difficulties are intensified in other group projects, where several contributors join their parts together in one document and in most instances the parts do not match. Moreover, in the contemporary digital reports, figures and images may occasionally be included. Nevertheless, uncontrolled insertion of unethical or unacceptable images may affect academic integrity. In this way, not only do the quality of the content have to be properly formatted, but also the possibility to avoid the incorporation of unethical content into the academic records. As automation, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing become increasingly more dependable, there is a high demand on a smart solution that can automatize formatting, comply with ethical standards, and offer an opportunity to allow the user to define the formatting needs in flexible ways.

heading: Problem Statement
content: The existing procedure of report creating is ineffective, prone to errors, and does not help the students to concentrate on their research quality. The vast majority of students do not have the technical knowledge to work with the more advanced formatting features of programs like Microsoft word or LaTeX. Consequently, they have to use manual adjustments that are quite repetitive and in most cases result in wastage of time, stress, and inconsistency of formatting. Moreover, the lack of an automated program that can address various institutional needs has presented a barrier to students who study in various academic settings. Another problem that keeps on reoccurring in a collaborative environment is the ability to merge various sections without losing formatting. Insufficiency of mechanisms used to guarantee ethical contents is another cause of concern. Learners will either add unprofessional images in their reports without knowing how, or they can do it deliberately, and this can result in both academic and professional punishment. Furthermore, the existing systems restrict the formatting to the manual mode of input and they do not consider innovations like speech-based instructions, which might make the process more user-friendly with people with varying needs. Therefore, an urgent demand is seen in the creation of the system that will be not only automated in formatting but also will make use of artificial intelligence to sort, arrange, and ethically control the material and promote various forms of interaction with the users.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: The offered project, which will be called Report Formatter, presents an AI- and machine learning-based program that will be used to automate the process of report formatting based on the templates specified by the user or institutions. The system will include: Admin Panel: It allows administrators to post and control format regulations like font styles, margins, table formats and heading structures. A custom template can be done by each university. AI-Powered Content Classification: Detecting attributes (heading, subheading, tables, images, captions, references) and formats them accordingly Ethical Image Detection: The system incorporates an AI model, which is capable of differentiating between ethical and unethical images. In case of an inappropriate or unethical image posted, the system will make sure that it is not included in the report, thus making sure that one does not go against academic and professional standards. Voice-Enabled Formatting Requirements: The users and administrators will be able to set formatting requirements by speech recognition using a microphone. This natural language processing capability renders the system more usable and easy to use especially when the user finds it more comfortable or needs to use voice interactivity as opposed to using handwriting. Student Application: This will enable students to post raw data (Word, PDF or plain text) and get a well formatted report according to the template of their campus. Specialized: Grammar checking, plagiarism checking, table of contents auto-generated, audio and table numbering, section recognition, version control, collaboration, and multilingual. Security Measures: It has data security and privacy measures which have been incorporated in order to secure sensitive academic work with the use of encryption and local storage. There is also live preview, with students being able to see changes in formatting on the fly, just like on platforms like LaTeX like Overleaf. Combining all these features, the solution is expected to offer a complete platform that is not confined to mere formatting and can improve the academic writing overall.

heading: Expected Outcomes
content: Application of Report Formatter system should bring about some gains: Time Savings: The automation of the repetitive format process will save the students much time so that they can be able to spend the time on creating the content and conducting research. Consistency and Accuracy: With automated formatting, the problem of human error will be removed, and the strict adherence to the requirements of the institution will be ensured. Ethical Protections: The unethical image detection feature can be used to keep academic reports professional, ethical and devoid of unprofessional content. Increased Accessibility - Speech-based input should allow users to create formatting rules via the voice, which will make the system more inclusive and easier to use. Improved Quality: Grammar correction and plagiarism detector features will help in bettering the quality and originality of reports. Collaboration Support: Teamwork in academic projects will be simplified with such features as version control and collaboration between people. Flexibility and Adaptability: The system will support the different formatting rules and languages and therefore can be applicable across the various institutions and regions. Flexibility: Compatibility with other academic submissions platforms, such as Word, PDF, and LaTeX document export capabilities will make it flexible. Data Security: Vigorous privacy protocols will ensure that sensitive student reports are safe and they are not abused. The purpose of this Report Formatter is, finally, to become a smart assistant to the students, researchers and institutions by creating a linkage between the content development, ethical adherence and professionalism. Using artificial intelligence, the system will not only enhance effectiveness of report writing, but also establish new levels of academic productivity, inclusiveness, and quality.

heading: Related Work
content: Document formatting automation is a new discipline that touches on Natural Language Processing (NLP), document layout analysis, and rule-based systems. Various commercial and academic solutions have tried to solve sections of this issue, but there exists little in the way of a widespread, template-driven, AI-assisted, academic report solution. Commercial word processors Powerful in their styling capabilities and templates, Microsoft Word and Google Docs need to be used manually. They are not smart enough to guess the framework of the unstructured academic text. Users have to apply formatting, which creates errors and inconsistency in longer reports. Overleaf and LaTeX In academia, Overleaf, a LaTeX cloud-based editor, is being widely used due to its strong typesetting features and active collaboration functionality [1]. Nevertheless, it involves the user learning how to use LaTeX, an important barrier to entry to many non-technical students. Although it is the best at generating well-structured reports, it does not offer AI flexibility in response to customer requirements. AI-driven text models GPT-based models, including ChatGPT, are able to produce and occasionally organize text but not be used to adhere to more complicated text formatting conventions, including margins, page breaks, or caption position. They also do not have a specific pipeline of analyzing document layout and adherence to formatting. Document Layout Analysis (DLA) DLA research is very relevant. Some projects like LayoutLM (Microsoft) [2] and DocBank [3] are based on deep learning to recognize textual and visual characteristics to understand the structure of the documents (titles, authors, paragraphs, etc.). These models are the basis of technology of our classification module but are research oriented as opposed to being implemented as end user academic tools. Content quality tools Grammatically and Turnitin are adjacent solutions. Grammarly prioritizes grammar, clarity, and tone recommendations [4] whereas Turnitin is the default plagiarism detection engine in the industry [5]. Nevertheless, both of them do not offer automatic formatting and adherence to institutional templates. Template engines Document creation systems such as Jinja or Apache POI are programmatic methods of document creation, where template documents are filled in with information. They are helpful with automation but not adaptive because they are unable to process unstructured academic material intelligently and correlate it with templates without human-defined rules. Automated format research A prototype of an NLP-based formatting system, which can be used to process documents and execute some rules automatically, was described by Islam & Rahman (2022) [6]. Although this is proof of its feasibility, the model is not extensible and fails to cover such sophisticated options as detecting ethics in images or speech-driven interaction. Ethical/unethical image detection Professional and academic integrity can be undermined by the uncontrolled incorporation of unethical or inappropriate pictures. Research in computer vision can be a good solution to this field. Image classification Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), ResNet, multimodal networks like CLIP [7] are examples of models that have been shown to have high precision in image classification tasks. Such systems are able to recognize inappropriate or irrelevant content and they are thus appropriate to be included in academic formatting software to maintain ethical standards. Speeches and voice interaction Speech recognition can be used to improve accessibility in formatting systems. The studies of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and intent classification, including Graves et al. (2006) [8], allow mapping natural speech to actions. New developments such as Google Speech-to-Text API and Whisper prove the accuracy of the transcription, and voice-powered formatting is possible and useful to the academic software with inclusivity. The project is expected to make an integration of all these disparate domains - DLA, NLP, template engines, computer vision, ASR and writing assistance tools into one user friendly application that is specifically tailored to an academic scenario, which currently there is a gap in the existing ecosystem of writing tools.

heading: Architecture
content: The architecture of the AI-based FYP Report Formatter is represented in this diagram (Figure 1), as well as the interaction between its key components. The system has four major components: Frontend (Desktop Application): Students utilize a cross-platform desktop use that has been developed on Flutter. They are able to view the ready output and post unrefined report material. Templates are also controlled by the administrators using the frontend. Backend (Python and AI Models): Supervises claims of formatting, plagiarism, and grammar, assignments categorization and AI-inspired propositions. Database (PostgreSQL): It holds in the PostgreSQL database; User data, version history, templates used to format data to different colleges, report data, which are scalable and satisfies the ACID. External Integrations: Exports both LaTeX/Pandoc to high quality and optional plagiarism APIs and AI categorization using spaCy and Hugging Face Transformers. The diagram describes these elements interaction by processing pipelines and API calls to achieve successful formatting and generation of reports.

heading: Methodology
content: The report formatter is  developed with a structured pipeline to ensure that it is properly formatted and that the content of the reports is classified based on data AI to identify the essential elements of the report. The interconnecting modules constituting the architecture (Figure 1) are each with a unique purpose. 1. Admin Panel Module: This module defines formatting templates, such as margins, table styles, placement of captions, hierarchy of headings, font size, and style. The templates are stored in the Template Database. 2. User Module(Students): This module handles registration, logins and submission of reports by students. It provides file upload services of text, PDF, and word documents. 3. File Upload and Parsing Module: It receives uploaded files and removes their raw content (text, tables and figures) and converts the information into a structured format to enable AI to process it. 4. AI Content Classification Module: The NLP model marks the sections (Heading 1, Heading 2, paragraphs, tables, photos, captions, references, etc.) of the text. It provides the Formatting Engine with directed content. 5. Formatting Engine Module: It uses standards of the university template to a content that is categorised and controls captions, margins, spacing, numbering and styles of headers. A draft report is generated. 6. Other AI Services: Plagiarism and grammar checker ensure the accuracy and originality. AI recommendations provides recommendations to missing portions of the paper, including the Conclusion. 7. Table of Contents/ Numbering Module: This will automatically generate a list of figures, list of tables and table of contents. It perfectly places captions (under the pictures, on the top of the tables). 8. Collaboration & Version Control Module: It allows a number of different students to post and merge sections. The rollback version history is also maintained. 9. Live Preview Module: It provides a preview of the organized report live. Students can see changes immediately, as it works with Overleaf. 10. Image Ethics Detection Module: This recognizes ethical or unethical images uploaded and beforehand inserts them, based on pre-trained computer vision models (e.g. ResNet, CLIP or custom CNNs). The moracious pictures pass, the immoral row. 11. Voice to Command Module: Speech recognition engine converts the spoken instructions into actions (e.g. bold heading, insert caption). It uses commands to format actions relying on ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) and NLP intent-classification.

heading: Introduction
content: The Secure Message Platform designed to provide people a secure and reliable communication platform. Nowadays, where cyberattacks and data breaches are happening more often security is the main focus of everyone. So, there is a great demand of such communication platform where data remains safe. The solution is centered on combining strong security measures such as data encryption, user authentication and access control along with a simple and user friendly design. Our goal is to provide data security not only for an individual but also for enterprises and institutions that manage sensitive information.

heading: Objectives
content: The Objectives include; to design and develop a trustable and secure communication platform and to ensure data protection using the principles of confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA).

heading: Objectives
content: So objective of our this project Encryption Software is that user should be to: Export a file through a file/folder picker along with a configured file so that we can manage user-defined paths. Then to be able to implement AES-256-GCM encryption which comes with a secure key derivation through using either PBKDF2 or Argon2id. Further, to enable automatic backup scheduling (daily/weekly) through the system’s built-in scheduling tool like Windows Task Scheduler or cron jobs. To record each saved backup versions together with its timestamp, which will then enable the restoration of older copies within the retention period. Then we also set a retention policy that automatically deletes backup copies which are older than the defined timeframe by the user, e.g., more than 4 days.

heading: Introduction
content: GoMate aims to deliver a reliable, cost effective and user friendly solution for urban transportation.It is inspired by popular ride-booking services like Uber and Careem, but offers unique features that make travelling more convenient and more efficient. The app will serve a dual purpose: Users are offered the choice of booking either a private ride or a ride sharing option, in which they can share rides with others headed in the same direction. This ride-sharing feature will match users based on a proximity radius or route alignment, so that deviation from the original route is minimal for drivers. GoMate focuses on efficient route management and minimal driver detours, which will promise time and cost efficient solution for both riders and drivers. For users who want to send packages across the city, GoMate will also include an additional parcel delivery feature. The aim of this feature is to meet the increasing need for fast and flexible local delivery options. The development of GoMate involves multiple sub-tasks, which contribute to the app’s functionality and user experience. Many of the key sub-tasks include designing a scalable backend to handle complex ride-matching algorithms. Real time location tracking and route visualization will be provided by the app using Google Maps, with updates on the rider’s and driver’s positions in real time. Other components of the project involve developing a responsive frontend to provide a smooth user experience across both iOS and Android platforms.

heading: Related Work
content: Some of the most famous apps with the concept of ride sharing have become leaders in their field, changing the transport services and providing the population with accessible and comfortable means of transport. Uber  has presented affordable and expensive versions of services, real-time tracking, and estimated fares of a trip. It has a dynamic rate-calculation model that is based on demand and supply which ensures availability all the time. However, some of the disadvantages include high peak rates for service provision as well as issues to do with fare satisfaction for drivers. Careem  operates as an app with ride hailing service, fare calculation and sharing service along with other services that include food and package delivery. It works according to geographical regions and has a reward program for the frequent users. However, it lacks adequate delivery service to customers in local areas and sometimes experiences glitches. Lyft  is centered on giving a pleasant driver and passenger experience and ride choices and encouraging shared rides for the environment. Indeed, it focuses on the driver’s feedback and electric vehicle using. However, it has limited global reach and higher costs in some regions which reduces its competitiveness. InDrive   have a very unique feature that passengers and drivers can freely set fares with one another, the company offers an adjustable price range. It also provides affordability since it eliminates standard fares charges. However, there are many problems such as inconsistency of price expectations and conflicts between users. Bykea  focuses majorly on motor bike ride hailing, parcel delivery services and mobile money products for working in populous cities. It relies on motorcycles for efficient and cheap services. Currently it is focused on bikes only and does not have options for car or auto-rickshaw transportation which significantly narrows down its range of customers. Bolt  has convenient services such as ride sharing, food delivery, scooter services all of which are cheap with emphasis on quick delivery. It advertises itself with real time tracking and competitive prices with the aim of attracting the users. However, being able to standardize service delivery across the various regions is still a major issue. Yango  offers first and last-mile transportation services that are cheap and include local payment options and the ability to monitor the ride in real time. It aims at achieving wider outreach and the modular design allows implementation in less developed areas and even in small cities. Yet, it does not possess highly developed riding algorithm matching that may have an impact on the consumer level. DiDi  has many services that are customized to serve the Asian and the Latin American population like ride hailing, bike sharing and food delivery. It applies data science and analytics for the pairing of riders to the nearest driver. But it comes across legal bottlenecks and issues concerning data privacy in some of the relevant markets. Grab  combines mobility, delivery, and fintech in one application. It adapts a localized strategy to achieve that. However, drawbacks include high cost and at times, the application slows down during certain periods in a day. Ola  offers various car categories for its clients, starting from auto rickshaw and ending with electric cars. It employs price discrimination and incentives to drivers to guarantee that a car is always available. However, it does not have a proper customer support service, and sometimes fails to provide enough drivers.

heading: Motivation
content: Our motivation comes from the need to offer better flexible and environmentally sustainable transport  and logistics services. We observe that traffic density, increased fuel demands and prices for individual services require the creation of an application that offers vital functions for effective travel and delivery needs. GoMate focuses on addressing these factors that remain a hurdle, by aiming at designing a platform that would acquire efficiency, convenience and reduce cost for consumer through the introduction of shared rides. Importance of problem: The current world transport requirement is tied to a demand for mobility and delivery services that are not adequately solved by existing solutions while meeting the challenging environmental targets. The problem areas include aggravation of emissions  , traffic jam , and accessibility problems that require a solution which enables one to overcome the challenges and provide viable alternatives to access the options. Meeting this need is important from the point of increasing the effectiveness of transport and excluding possible negative effects on the environment. Reason for undertaking the Project: We chose this project because it presents an opportunity to have a positive contribution towards transportation and logistics. Through the development of GoMate, we focus on pushing towards better and more efficient mobility solutions that suit contemporary consumers’ wants. This project provides a very good avenue for people to implement and work on real technology that is also helpful to the public and at the same time helps influence responsible usage of vehicles.

heading: Objectives
content: Provide Multi-Modal Services: Design an app with choice of personal one-on-one driving service, car sharing and delivery service. Implement an Intelligent Matching System: Development of a system that associates the users within the shortest distance and their direction of travel, to further reduce distance covered and improve on the convenience of consumers of ride sharing services. Integrate Advanced Route Optimization: Integration of geolocation service and the best route planning algorithm to determine the shortest, most cost effective route that shall in turn benefit both drivers and users through shorter time and fuel consumption. Ensure Real-Time Updates: Display of real time GPS tracking, distance based fare structure and live status updates that will keep users informed at all times in a journey or delivery. Enhance Urban Mobility and Sustainability: To build sustainable networks for greener cities by endorsing the sharing of the means of transportation to help decrease the traffic jam and pollutant emissions in cities. Deliver Secure and Reliable Parcel Services: Allow users to deliver packages rapidly and safely within some regions make an efficient, supplementary logistics solution to the application.

heading: Methodology
content: The development of the "GoMate" ride-sharing app follows a structured approach, ensuring smooth integration of key components to deliver an efficient and user-friendly experience. The system architecture as shown in figure 1 is organized into interconnected modules, each performing a specific function User Module: This module manages user registration, login, profile information, and access permissions. It connects to the User Data Storage to store and retrieve user information securely. Ride Booking Module: This module is responsible for receiving the user ride requests and facilitating ride booking by having the user select pickup and drop-off location. It acts as the entry point for users requesting rides and connects with the Location Module to get accurate coordinates for ride management. Location Module: The location module interacts with mapping services to get the coordinates for pickup and drop-off points. This module also determines the current location of users and drivers, feeding this data into both the Tracking & Notification Module and the Ride Sharing decision-making process. Ride Sharing Decision: This decision point determines whether a ride request can be shared with another user based on proximity and similar routes. If the criteria for ride-sharing is met, the Ride Matching Module is activated; otherwise, the Ride Management Module handles it as a single ride. Ride Matching Module: This module identifies potential ride matches for shared rides based on location, route, and timing constraints. The module works with the Route Optimization Module to determine the most efficient route for multiple pickups and drop-offs. Route Optimization Module: This module uses Google OR-Tools to calculate the optimal route to minimize travel time and cost for both shared and individual rides. Route optimization ensures efficient fuel usage and helps the driver avoid unnecessary detours to improve service quality. Ride Management Module: This module manages the overall process of each ride. It is also responsible for updating ride statuses and handling cancellations. It communicates with both the Tracking & Notification Module for real-time status updates and the Database to store ride information in Ride Data Storage. Tracking & Notification Module: This module provides real-time updates ride status, arrival time, and notifications for changes. It uses data from the Location Module to track the ride and keep both parties informed. Fare Calculation Module: The fare calculation module calculates the total cost of each ride based on distance, time, and ride-sharing options. This module takes input from the Route Optimization Module to accurately calculate the cost, which is displayed to the user before confirming the ride. Database (User Data Storage and Ride Data Storage): The database stores all user and ride data. User profiles and ride history are stored in User Data Storage and Ride Data Storage, respectively, ensuring data is available for ride management, history tracking, and future reference.

heading: Abstract
content: Due to social media's widespread influence in modern society, there has been much discussion about how social media use affects health. This report offers a thorough analysis of the relationship between social media usage and various aspects of health. By synthesizing research findings and analysis, the study aims to clarify the intricate relationship between social media platforms and individual well-being. The study's goal is to identify the positive and negative effects of social media on health outcomes, including social, mental, and physical dimensions. The executive summary, which uses a qualitative approach, provides a nuanced perspective free of acronyms or jargon, making it easy to understand for readers with a wide range of backgrounds. Key findings indicate that while social media facilitates communication, connectivity, and access to health-related information, it also engenders challenges such as cyberbullying, addiction, and unrealistic social comparisons. The report also discusses the possible effects of social media on mental health disorders like anxiety, depression, and problems with self-esteem.

heading: Introduction
content: Social media has an undeniable impact on modern society, influencing all facets of interpersonal relationships and social structures. But amid its widespread use is a landscape full of complexities and implications that need careful examination. This introduction sets out to analyze the complex effects of social media with the goal of shedding light on these effects and offering understanding of their significant influence. Individual behaviors, cultural norms, and communication patterns have all undergone an unparalleled shift as a result of social media platforms' remarkable growth. Worries about how this change will affect people's mental health, relationships with others, consumer behavior, public opinion, economic dynamics, and cultural phenomena are also growing along with this change. In light of the consequences of a world growing more digitally interconnected, it is critical for society to comprehend and manage these complexities. The goals of this conversation are multiple: To examine social media's complex effects on modern society from a number of angles. To shed light on the opportunities and difficulties that come with social media in the digital age and promote a better comprehension of how it shapes social structures and human interactions. In order to grab readers' attention and emphasize the importance of more research into this developing phenomenon, the main conclusions and trends drawn from research, statistical data, and expert insights will be highlighted. To highlight the need of using thoughtful, nuanced methods and well-informed strategies to navigate the complexities of social media's impact on people and societies. In order to gather information for this discussion, a thorough evaluation of academic papers, empirical studies, statistical data, and professional opinions from reliable sources in the domains of technology, sociology, psychology, economics, and communication studies was conducted. In order to provide a comprehensive understanding of the subject matter, methodological approaches included systematic literature reviews, quantitative analysis of survey data, qualitative analysis of case studies, and synthesis of various perspectives. heading: Introduction
content: Code smells are not bugs of a program but poor implemen- tation choices that may signify the weakness of software design. Although it is a surface indication of code structure, code smells may expose a deeper problem in a software system. The presence of code smells may increase the risk of failure, make software difficult to maintain, and introduce potential technique debt in the future. Detecting code smells has become increasingly important for software evolution. More than 20 kinds of code smells have been identified in thousands of real-world projects. Palomba et al. [1] conducted a survey with 162 developers and discovered that more than 90% of developers focus on prevalent code smells (such as feature envy, god class, and long method) rather than seldom- used code smells, such as brain class (BC) and brain method (BM). BC/BM code smells usually have numerous structural branches and deeply recursive invocations, which disobeys the proportion rule and increases the risk of failure. ∗ Corresponding author. E-mail address: zhangyang@hebust.edu.cn (Y. Zhang). Many works have been conducted to identify code smells since the automated detection tool was originally proposed [2]. Traditional approaches employ heuristic-based approaches [3,4] by computing a collection of metrics. A predefined threshold is set to distinguish between smelly samples and nonsmelly sam- ples. However, code snippets with different behaviors may use the same metric and consequently have a totally different code smells. Furthermore, choosing a proper threshold requires ex- pertise. Lacking experience and holding potential bias have a negative impact on making the appropriate decision. Some re- searchers have improved code smells detection by employing machine learning (ML) techniques, such as K-means [5], sup- port vector machine (SVM) [6], and naive bayes [7]. However, these techniques suffer from insufficient feature extraction [8]. As a result, the accuracy of their results is not satisfactory. In recent years, some researchers have begun to detect code smells by leveraging deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural network(CNN) [9], long short-term memory(LSTM) [10], and residual network(ResNet) [11]. Most works initially build a dataset by extracting features from the source code and then train a deep learning model to obtain a classifier. Deep-learning-based approaches significantly improve the accuracy of code smell de- tection. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2022.109737 0950-7051/© 2022 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved. Y. Zhang, C. Ge, S. Hong et al. Knowledge-Based Systems 255 (2022) 109737 Although many works on code smell detection have been conducted, several problems remain open. First, existing approaches mainly focus on structural features of the source code, while semantic features are prone to being disregarded. Consequently, the features learned by the model may be biased. Second, existing works lack a unified dataset for different code smells. Additionally, the deep-learning-based model can be further optimized. Third, the existing data en- hancement algorithm synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) [12] is not visualized. Some samples generated by SMOTE probably disturb the boundary between positive samples and negative samples (illustrated in Section 3). To address these problems, this paper proposes a novel ap- proach named DeleSmell to detect code smells based on a deep learning model. To increase the number of positive samples, a refactoring tool is developed to automatically transform nons- melly items into smelly items in real-world projects. DeleSmell extracts both structural features by iPlasma [13] and semantic features by latent semantic analysis (LSA) [14] and word2vec [15]. Thus, a dataset with more than 200,000 samples is con- structed from 24 real-world projects. DeleSmell builds a deep neural network model, including a CNN branch and gate recurrent unit(GRU)-attention branch. The final classification is conducted by an SVM. In the experimentation, the effectiveness of De- leSmell is evaluated by answering seven research questions. The experimental results show that DeleSmell improves the accu- racy of BC/BM code smells detection by up to 4.41% compared with existing approaches, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: • A novel approach named DeleSmell is proposed to detect code smells based on the deep learning model and LSA. • A refactoring tool is developed to automatically generate positive samples of the dataset. • A dataset with more than 200,000 samples is built from 24 real-world projects. • Many experiments have been conducted to evaluate the ef- fectiveness of DeleSmell by answering seven research ques- tions. The remainder of the paper is structured as follows: Section 2 examines related works. Section 3 illustrates the motivation of our work. Section 4 presents an overview of DeleSmell and the design of each component. The experimental setup and results are reported in Section 5. This paper is concluded in Section 6.

heading: Abstract
content: Skin health is an essential aspect of overall well-being, yet many individuals struggle to access personalized skincare guidance. Existing skincare applications are often limited to brand-driven product marketing or provide generic solutions that fails to address diverse skin tones, local environment factors, and individual lifestyles. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes SkinIQ- an AI-powered skincare assistant. The system will analyze user skin images using computer vision models, provide quiz-based assessments for users unable to upload photos, and recommend skincare products filtered by ingredients, budget, and local availability. Furthermore, the system will integrate holistic lifestyle advice including diet, hydration, and sleep, while enabling progress tracking and community interaction. By combining artificial intelligence, dermatological insights, and contextual awareness (e.g., climate, allergies), SkinIQ aims to deliver a personalized, safe, and accessible skincare experience. Holistic advice including diet, hydration, sleep, and seasonal skincare routines. Progress tracking via before/after comparisons and habit reminders. Community interaction and education to build user engagement and trust. By combining these features, SkinIQ will offer a unique, localized, and user- centric platform.

A product recommendation system integrated with a local skincare product database (PKR-based) A lifestyle advisory module providing hydration, sleep, and seasonal advice. heading: Introduction
content: Higher education has become one of the essential elements in  modeling individual occupational paths, socio-economic growth and international standing. World university ranking system has become a crucial mechanism for students, researchers, policymakers, and educational establishments as nowadays, globally universities are appraised on behalf of their academic reputation, research environment, staff competency, student faculty ratio, international outlook etc. World's well known university ranking Systems such as QS, THE, ARWU has provided uniform criteria that affects the organizational reputation and decision making of an individual. These systems have significant influence on Potential learners  identenfying their right choice of instituation, researchers exploring alliances and  government formulating academic policies. Existing global ranking systems , regardless of their significance, uses a one-size-fits-all methodology that focuses on standardized benchmark overlooking the needs of varirty of users. As is well known, QS focuses on academic and employer reputation, faculty/student ratio, citation per faculty and international faculty and student ratio, however, THE gives weight to teaching quality, research environment and quality, industry impact and international outlook. In the same way, ARWU prioritizes nobles award winners and highly citied researchers, publications and per capita performance. These indicators yield informative outcomes yet they they might overlook the preferences that academics and individual students finds important. A student focusing on career development prioritizes employer reputation, however, a student focusing on scholary work gives more weight reasech environment and quality. In this way, customized preferences are neglected and stakeholders are left with one uniform ranking result that unable to reflect the needs of variety of users having diverse priorities. The motivation for this project appears from the natural limitation of fixed ranking systems and the need for a personalized one. Global rankings effects academic and professional choices yearly, yet they fail to feed to multiple individual choices . For example, a student following research may focus on faculty skillfulness and publication impact, whereas another focused on capability may value alumni success and employer recognition more. This requires the need for flexible judging tools . Moreover, fast AI development has made it possible to analyze user behaviours and preferences which helps to generate data-driven personalized recommendation. Using Ai for adaptive university ranking can transform how students , researchers and policy-makers make higher education planning. This project is important because it fulfiils user needs and wants making ranking more personal and meaningful. It keeps the trust and accuracy of existing systems but adds a human touch, something that helps people make choices and that actually fit their own needs and preferences. The basic purpose of this project is to compose and create a Personalized University Ranking and Recommendation Platform that allows users to create custom-made university rankings and receive AI-driven suggestions. The aim of the system is to: Analyze ranking data from QS, THE, and ARWU without mixing their methodologies; Enable users to assign custom weights to factors such as research, faculty-student ratio, and employability; and Provide AI-based university recommendations adapted to user profiles and preferences. The scope of this project includes developing a multi-platform application (web and mobile), putting into practice a recommendation engine using AI techniques, and offering envisaged outputs to aid decision-making. However, the project does not aim to modify or merge the original ranking methodologies of QS, THE, or ARWU. Instead, it focuses completely on analyzing and deciphering their data to enhance user understanding and personalized capability. This project aims at the implementation of a Personalized University Ranking and Recommendation platform that uses datasets from leading ranking providers QS, THE and ARWU, while maintaining their methodologies discretely. Rather than combining criteria across datasets, the system will allow users to select a ranking dataset of their choice, and then customize results based on what parameters are available and assign weights to them within that dataset. In addition to basic customization, the system will also incorporate an AI-based recommendation engine that will learn user profiles, expressed preferences and implicit behavior to recommend universities that are a cultural and financial match for the user's academic, financial or professional goals. This blend of custom weighting and AI-powered recommendations will result in a hybrid solution that combines transparency with intelligent personalization. The indented result will be a functional cross-platform application designed to deliever personalized ranking result along with an integrated AI- based recommendation engine. User will have the ability to: Select from the different ranking providers while preserving the authenticity of evaluation methodology. Modify weigthing parameter within the dataset chosen according to user-specific choices Gain access to AI-powered recommendations that analyze both direct and indirect user needs. Seek to develop ranking results that will corresponds more closely with academic, financial or career objectives. View reports and charts that clearly show how preferences and AI suggestions affects the results. This project seeks to develop  a clear, dynamic, and user-centered platform that meaningfully strenghtens decision-making in academic planning, by preserving the reliability of existing ranking systems while integrating both a customization layer and an AI-driven recommendation module.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Lack of personalization in current global university ranking systems like QS, THE, and ARWU results in a large gap between standardized metrics of evaluation and diverse individual user preferences. The systems provide consistent results that do not consider disparate priorities like research quality, affordability, teaching excellence, or employability. Consequently, learners and scholars can rarely determine most suitable institutions in accordance with their objectives, resulting in less-than-optimal academic and professional choices. Existing approaches are based on inflexible, one-size-fits-all weighting systems and do not utilize adaptive intelligence capable of inspecting user action or preferences. This shortcoming makes the provision of an intelligent, user-responsive system imperative with both existing rankings' credibility and added flexibility, and AI-powered personalization. Solving this issue will make decision-making in higher education stronger and offer a more meaningful and transparent evaluation framework.

heading: Objectives
content: The main goal of this project is to design and develop an AI-based web and mobile platform that provides personalized university ranking insights by analyzing global ranking systems such as QS, THE, and ARWU according to user-defined preferences. The following specific objectives have been defined to achieve this goal: To analyze and extract key parameters from major global university ranking datasets (QS, THE, ARWU) for comprehensive comparison and evaluation. To develop a unified analytical framework that interprets ranking parameters according to user priorities using normalization and weighting techniques. To build an AI-powered recommendation system that dynamically suggests universities best aligned with individual academic, financial, and regional preferences. To design and implement an interactive user interface for web and mobile platforms using React.js and React Native for seamless accessibility. To integrate a real-time database (Supabase) for managing user profiles, search history, and preference data securely. To enable push notifications and updates using Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for user engagement and ranking insights. To monetize the platform through Google AdSense (web) and AdMob (mobile) while maintaining an ad-friendly user experience. To evaluate system performance and user satisfaction through testing, feedback, and measurable accuracy of AI-based recommendations.

heading: Related Work
content: University ranking systems have a big impact on student decision-making and institutional reputation, they have been the focus of research and discussion for many years. Early attempts at ranking universities date back to the 1980s when the U.S. News & World Report introduced its college ranking system in the United States, primarily based on reputation surveys and statistical indicators . Since then, global ranking systems such as the QS World University Rankings, Times Higher Education (THE), and the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) have become the most significatn sources of institutional comparison. These rankings have shaped higher education by providing standardized indicators of performance, but their methodologies remain subject to criticism for lack of transparency and adaptability. QS World University Rankings:QS ranking system is based on the six parameters: academic reputation, employer reputation, faculty/student ratio, citations per faculty, international faculty ratio, and international student ratio . Focus on academic reputation, derived from surveys of academics worldwide, has made QS rankings highly significant in shaping perceptions of quality. However, critics argue that the reliance on survey-based data introduces subjectivity and potential bias, particularly against lesser-known institutions in developing regions .More, QS does not allow users to adjust the weight of these parameters, makes the system rigid for students with different preferences. Times Higher Education (THE) Rankings:THE ranking system focuses on 13 performance indicators grouped into five categories: teaching, research, citations, international outlook, and industry income . Unlike QS, THE covers a broader set of parameters that captures the  both academic and non-academic aspects of  the universities. Although THE takes a comprehensive approach, THE’s weighting system is fixed, meaning that teaching and research indicators may overshadow criteria that are more relevant to specific user groups, such as internationalization or employability . Studies suggest that despite providing insightful information, THE is still unavailable to users who want to customize ranking outputs according to their  personal goals . Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU): ARWU, developed by Shanghai Jiao Tong University, highlights research superiority by measuring Nobel Prize achievements, highly cited researchers, and publications in top journals . While ARWU is recognized for its impartiality, its heavy dependency on research indicators makes it less applicable for students essentially concerned with teaching quality, affordability, or employability. The system, like QS and THE, does not support customer-centeric personalization of ranking results. Research shows that ARWU’s methodology favors established institutions in developed countries, thus limiting its usefulness for students in other contexts . Criticism of Existing Rankings Scholars have censured global rankings for promoting a consistent and highly competitive model of higher education that often miss local contexts and individual user needs . Marginson  argues that global rankings strengthen reputational hierarchies rather than providing applicable perception for varying stakeholders. Additionally, Hazelkorn  highlights that uniform ranking models can entice students by highlighting reputation over practical ruminations such as financial cost, teaching quality, or alignment with personal academic goals.

heading: Abstract
content: Pakistan's economy depends heavily on agriculture, however rural farmers do not have access to many advantages, such as weather information, current expertise, and scientific farming practices. Traditional methods alongside literacy issues and poor connectivity hinder farmers from applying innovative solutions, and hence they face low returns and economic losses. The biggest problem is that farmers usually do not receive timely information regarding government schemes, correct crop calendars, and scientific information regarding soil and irrigation. Additionally, illiteracy limits their access to text-based programs, and in remote locations, unreliable internet makes online-only solutions unfeasible. To overcome these challenges, this project puts forth PakFasal, a Flutter-based mobile application that offers localized learning content, voice-to-text communication for uneducated farmers, offline data storage, and an immediate marketplace to bridge farmers with businesses. The app also incorporates weather prediction and IoT-based soil sensors (pH level and moisture) to provide real-time field information. Some of the expected outcomes are better decision-making in crop management, maximized water use and fertilizers, lowered reliance on intermediaries, and increased farmer participation. By combining mobile technology, voice interfaces, and IoT sensors, the app aims to empower farmers with knowledge and tools that increase productivity and support sustainable agriculture.

heading: Problem Statement
content: The three key challenges faced by Pakistan's farmers are: (1) inability to get timely localized agriculture information, such as government programs, crop calendars, and disease management strategies, (2) literacy and connectivity issues since most farmers are illiterate or semi-literate and inhabit regions with weak internet connectivity, and (3) reliance on unscientific agriculture practices, wherein irrigation and use of fertilizers are done on a guesswork basis without any scientific inputs. There are currently existing mobile applications and SMS platforms that have tried to solve some of these problems, but none of these solutions have offline capabilities, real-time weather forecasting, or connectivity with low-cost IoT devices. In view of, a complete, focused on farmers solution is urgently needed. Farmers in Pakistan lack localized information, are illiterate, have connectivity issues, and have no access to intelligent, mostly offline, sensors (IoT) based decision support system DSS.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: To address these problems, this project proposes PAKFASAL, a mobile application developed in Flutter that provides agricultural education and decision support in a farmer-centric manner. The app will deliver tutorials, articles, and videos in multiple local languages, ensuring accessibility for farmers across Pakistan. A voice-to-text interface will allow illiterate farmers to interact with the app naturally, while offline caching will make content available even in low-connectivity regions. The system integrates real-time weather forecasting and IoT-based soil sensors (pH and moisture), offering actionable insights on irrigation scheduling and fertilizer usage. In addition, the app will feature a farmer–company marketplace to eliminate middlemen and a query portal where farmers can upload crop issues (text, voice, or pictures) for expert or AI-driven responses. Figure 1: A Use Case Diagram Of PAKFASAL

heading: Problem Statement
content: Farmers in Pakistan face a range of interrelated hurdles that highly impede agricultural productivity and sustainability. The first hurdle relates to the relatively timely and localized agricultural information informing such as government support programs, crop calendars, and disease/pest management practices. Farmers therefore cannot make informed choices without such information sources. The second hurdle relates to the many illiteracy and connectivity challenges. Many farmers are illiterate or semi-illiterate and live in rural locations where connectivity is the most inadequate. This blocks those individuals from using digital tools or accessing newer knowledge of practices and innovations. Additionally, many farmers remain committed to using traditional or un-scientific practices and often make decisions around irrigation, fertilizer and pest management from instinct instead of from supporting data or information. While some mobile apps or SMS applications exist to challenge some of these issues, little exists to provide offline tools or real-time weather forecasts or connect with cost-sensitive IoT devices. In this context, we need to produce a solution that is holistic, farmer-centred and that could be used, even in low-connectivity situations, to build on intelligent decision support systems (DSS) based on sensors.

heading: Objectives
content: The overall goal of the PAKFASAL project is the creation of an intelligent farm platform that will supply location-based precise recommendations to the farmer with an integrated Suggestion System and Decision Support System (DSS).The platform is designed to support famers at making decisions on which crops to use, time of planting, irrigation scheduling, and disease management by processing real-time information on current weather and soil conditions and local farming practices. heading: Abstract
content: With the rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, energy monitoring systems have evolved to offer more efficient, accurate, and accessible solutions. This project presents the design and implementation of an IoT-based intelligent three-phase energy analyzer capable of measuring and analyzing key electrical parameters in real time. The system utilizes the ESP32 microcontroller along with ZMPT101B voltage sensors and SCT100A current sensors to monitor phase-wise voltage, current, real power, reactive power, apparent power, power factor, frequency, phase angle, and cumulative energy consumption (kWh). The collected data is transmitted to the ThingSpeak cloud platform for real-time visualization and remote access. A user-friendly web dashboard has been developed to display the data graphically and numerically, allowing users to track energy usage trends, view reports, and download consumption history. Firebase Authentication is integrated to enable secure login and personalized access for each user. The system eliminates the limitations of conventional energy meters by offering enhanced analytical capabilities, remote accessibility, and phase-wise monitoring, making it suitable for both residential and industrial applications. The proposed solution contributes to energy awareness and efficiency by empowering users with detailed, actionable insights into their electricity consumption. heading: Introduction
content: Given that global energy demand is increasing, being smart about energy today is more valuable than ever. A lack of real-time tracking of both power generation and use has caused an energy crisis in Pakistan as well. One of the biggest challenges in Pakistan comes from energy crises which exist largely because energy use is not regularly tracked. That is even truer in industrial and commercial zones, as three-phase supply systems give more stability and efficiency. However, conventional meters are unable to provide us with the necessary information to look after and control the systems properly. Traditional energy meters only track total energy used and leave users unsure about how and why they use electricity. As technology keeps improving, energy management is now important for saving money, saving resources and supporting sustainability. One purpose of the IOT enabled smart energy analyzer is to help create lasting and effective energy solutions. Thanks to IoT, energy management will improve as you can access and analyze data from anywhere and see the results in real time. This project will develop a smart energy analyzer powered by IoT that measures usage and sends back additional information to the person using it. Because of this analyzer, consumers can check how much energy they use and how they can reduce it and their electric bill. Users can also see real-time data for every phase and review past data to lower their energy usage by knowing when to reduce energy.

heading: Problem Statement
content: In industrial and commercial settings, three-phase power networks are widely used, yet traditional energy meters offer only basic monitoring capabilities and lack real-time insights into critical parameters such as voltage, current, power factor, and various types of power (real, reactive, and apparent). This results in several challenges, including inefficient monitoring where anomalies like voltage imbalances and overloads go undetected, limited data accessibility due to the absence of remote access, poor energy optimization stemming from inadequate data, and the inability to integrate with modern smart energy management technologies. Therefore, there is a pressing need for an innovative, IoT-based system that bridges the gap between conventional energy monitoring and intelligent energy control by providing real-time data visualization, remote accessibility, and comprehensive analysis to enhance the performance and efficiency of three-phase systems. Such a system can empower users to make informed decisions, reduce energy waste, and improve operational reliability. By leveraging sensor integration and cloud-based dashboards, it enables proactive energy management from any location. Ultimately, this approach supports sustainability goals and aligns with the growing demand for smarter, more efficient energy solutions.

heading: Motivation
content: Because more energy is being used around the world and because we must be smarter about using energy, better energy management is essential. Because they are standard in industry and business, three-phase power systems depend on advanced tools to keep track of and analyze electrical data properly. Yet, classic energy meters do not give the detailed and real-time data needed to use energy most efficiently. This project is motivated by several important factors: Energy Efficiency: As costs for energy rise and we become more aware of the environment, optimizing how we use energy has become very important. A system with instant information and easy-to-use advice lets users locate energy-saving opportunities. Technological Advancements: Remote monitoring, data analysis and automation have all become possible because of IoT technology. IoT combined with energy analysis can turn traditional power management into an intelligent and flexible process. System Reliability: Damage and loss can occur in an industry when anomalies such as overloaded systems or a difference in voltages cause equipment to fail. Being able to monitor your systems in real time helps you find concerns early and make maintenance cheaper. Sustainability Goals: As we focus on sustainability, there is greater stress on using technologies that help save energy and protect the environment. An IoT-based energy analyzer helps meet these goals by promoting better energy use. Empowering Users: Helping users grasp how their energy consent is used helps them choose what actions to take, including reducing expenses, raising system performance or switching to renewable energy. To tackle these motivating factors, we are developing a strong, IoT-connected energy analyzer for three-phase systems that can help address modern issues in energy management.

heading: Objectives
content: The goal is to design and build an IoT smart energy analyzer for three-phase electrical systems. Our main objectives are: Real Time Monitoring: Users can view different electrical parameters including voltage and current of the different phases, real power, apparent power, reactive power, frequency, power factor, and energy. IoT Integration: Having an IoT system, users can look over and manage the energy analyzer from any place with a cloud portal. User-Friendly Web Interface: Allow them to use a web platform to check how much energy is being consumed in each of the three stages, review past data, analyze their energy consumption and decide on more energy-saving strategies. Enhanced Energy Efficiency: Help users to figure out which areas they use too much or too little energy. Sustainability and Efficiency: Help people manage their energy by introducing new practices that are environmentally friendly.

heading: Literature Review
content: The need to have efficient energy management, as well as fast-growing technology, has since given rise to the development of the traditional energy meters into smart energy analyzers. The current generation of the devices performs an important task, as it allows achieving accurate billing, constant 24/7 real-time monitoring, and the ability of integration with renewable energy sources. The use of smart energy analyzers combined with modern hardware devices, the IoT online services and network communication standards allows to ease the energy consumption monitoring and controlling process. Although they provide remarkable benefits associated with automation, data ease of access, and efficient functioning, they also have some challenges that include issues of privacy, reliance on constant internet access, and exorbitant costs of installation. The new developments in this area examine the enhancement of security, accuracy, and scalability of the system besides outlining the challenges. The literature shows the potential of smart energy analyzers to change energy management towards greater sustainability and sustainable management through the movement to smarter, and data-driven power systems.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: The monitoring system we have proposed for three-phase power works more effectively and in real time than traditional energy monitoring systems. This equipment makes it possible to understand essential electrical aspects which typical meters rarely do. A strong understanding of voltage, current, power (all types) and frequency is needed for three-phase systems in both commercial and industrial areas. The sensors and microcontrollers used now ensure the system is both accurate and reliable in collecting and managing data. The key performance indicators are computed by examining actual electrical data from voltage and current sensors. Sophisticated microcontrollers such as ESP32 help make processing data fast and let devices connect easily with cloud services. As a result, users can access current information remotely whenever they need it, thanks to the updates sent automatically. The integration of these features in the suggested system helps with energy monitoring and lets users benefit from improved ways to manage energy, lower costs and optimize the system. In monitoring and controlling energy in three-phase systems today, this is a necessary tool.

heading: Implementation
content: This chapter discusses the practical deployment of the IoT Enabled Smart Energy Analyzer for Three Phase Systems. This consisted of connecting sensors, preparing the firmware, live processing data and displaying it on ThingSpeak. The purpose was to use modern instrumentation for accurate, remote observation of important electrical signals during each phase of a power system.

heading: Conclusion
content: In our project, we developed and implemented a smart energy analyzer for a three-phase system using low-cost equipment and the Internet, making it possible for real-time monitoring. Combining the Wi-Fi features of ESP32 DevKit V1 with the ZMPT101B voltage sensor and the SCT100A current sensor allowed us to get and show data on power consumption on both a display and on ThingSpeak. The prototype for a single-phase circuit proved the approach and its transfer to a three-phase system verified our belief in the system’s flexibility and dependability. During development, making sure the sensors were correctly adjusted guaranteed they remained accurate, while using the open-source dashboard allowed users to see how much energy they used over time. The use of readily available tools makes it possible for the solution to be used broadly and affordably in residential, business and small-scale industrial environments.

heading: Future Work
content: As a result, this system forms a strong base for upcoming features such as auto fault detection, detailed analysis of energy use and predictive warnings for maintenance. It would be possible to enhance the system by detecting anomalies with machine learning, including support for solar panels and allowing the client to monitor from mobile apps. As a result, this project meets its target of helping users save energy and money, while also suggesting ways to make the grid more intelligent and connected so all stakeholders can base their decisions on helpful data.
