heading: Abstract
content: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) is a popular software engineering practice that specifies system behavior in natural language, fostering collaboration between developers, testers, and business stakeholders. By separating specifications from implementations, BDD enables clearer communication, better requirement validation, and improved test-driven workflows, making it a widely adopted approach in modern quality assurance. However, BDD test suites are not free from challenges, as poorly designed scenarios often lead to “test smells,” which undermine readability, increase brittleness, and reduce long-term maintainability. Existing research primarily addresses test smells at the implementation level, leaving the specification level underexplored due to the complexity of analyzing natural language. To address this gap, this project proposes an NLP-based approach that preprocesses BDD specifications through tokenization, stopword removal, and lemmatization, and extracts linguistic, contextual, and domain-specific features such as part-of-speech tags, named entities, BDD keywords, action words, and parameters. These features are then mapped to corresponding test code elements using an NLP-driven algorithm, which simultaneously enables systematic detection of test smells like duplication, ambiguity, and overly complex steps. Empirical case studies are employed to validate the model, demonstrating improved accuracy in mapping specifications to implementations and enhanced smell detection capabilities. The expected outcomes include better traceability between specifications and tests, improved test maintainability, and higher overall quality assurance in BDD environments, contributing a novel methodology that integrates NLP into automated software testing practices.

heading: Introduction
content: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) is a software development methodology. It was first presented by Daniel et al., on the idea to clearly define what the software should do before creating it. This method avoids confusion by clearly stating what the software should do, helping it meet business requirements and keeping everyone on the same page. The two levels of tests  are the implementation level and the specification level as shown in Figure 1. A Domain-Specific Language (DSL) like Gherkin is used to write natural language-based scenarios at the specification level. This allows requirement engineers, developers, and testers to all have an understanding of the system. Developers write test code to make sure the system does what the written requirements say. BDD is used a lot in research and business because it helps everyone on the team stay connected and understand each other . Among the most widely used tools that support creating, organizing, and running BDD tests are frameworks like Robot , SpecFlow, Cucumber, and Gauge. These frameworks preserve a direct link to executable test code while enabling the specification of system behavior in natural language. Although BDD enhances system validation and communication, its two-level architecture creates new difficulties for test design and upkeep. In particular, it becomes more difficult to guarantee uniformity and quality at both levels when specifications and implementations are kept apart. One of the major challenges in BDD is the emergence of test smells, which are symptoms of poor test design that reduce readability, increase brittleness, and complicate maintenance . Test smells have been studied extensively in unit testing and code-level implementations , where automated detection tools exist to identify common smells like Assertion Roulette or Eager Test. However, most of these studies are limited to the implementation level and do not address the unique challenges of natural language specifications. For example, a specification scenario may include duplicated steps, vague action descriptions, or ambiguous requirements that introduce specification-level smells. Detecting such smells is difficult due to the flexible and natural language-based nature of BDD specifications . Although previous research has explored requirement smells using Although NLP-based methods  exist, we have seen limited application of similar methods in the analysis of BDD scenarios. This ultimately results in test suites that gradually lose their quality, reducing their ability to ensure correctness of software behavior, and increasing long-term maintenance costs. All of the test smell definitions used in this proposal, are taken from a systematic mapping study of test smell detection tools . By introducing an NLP-based method to map BDD specifications to their corresponding implementation tests and automatically identify test smells at the specification level, this project seeks to address these issues. Tokenisation, stopword removal, and lemmatisation are used to preprocess BDD specifications at the start of the methodology. While domain-specific features like BDD keywords ("Given," "When," "Then"), action words, and parameters are found to improve the mapping process, linguistic features like dependency parses, named entities, and part-of-speech tags are extracted to capture the grammatical structure of scenarios. An NLP-driven mapping algorithm that uses similarity metrics like cosine similarity on vectorised features is then used to align these extracted features with test code elements. This alignment creates traceability from natural language scenarios to implementation tests, as well as helps identify smells, such as duplication of steps, overly complicated scenarios. The project aims to deliver a proven approach to improve the quality of BDD tests, focusing on traceability and identifying test smells. This approach will be evaluated through real-world BDD projects using empirical methods. Anticipated results include higher maintainability of test suites, reduced brittleness in test cases, and improved readability of specifications. Furthermore, this research contributes to advancing automated quality assurance by integrating NLP with BDD testing practices. The success criteria will be based on measurable improvements in smell detection accuracy, successful mapping of specifications to implementations, and evidence of improved maintainability through refactoring efforts. Ultimately, this project provides a practical solution that not only identifies quality issues early at the specification level but also strengthens the overall reliability of BDD test frameworks.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Many test smells have been introduced in the literature but with a limited scope, i.e., their definitions are limited to Unit-testing. Multi-level test cases in BDD have not been considered during defining test smells. Up to our knowledge, we have not found any study that discuss the scope of test smells in BDD domain. There might be a reason that this direction has been less focused by the researchers, maybe the way we write specifications in BDD. For example, the specification writer has freehand to write test specifications in natural language by not even following any syntax writing standards. As specification syntax varies from person to person, which also made it difficult to define test smell definitions at this level. That’s why, its hard to define test smell definitions at this level. Similarly, another very famous BDD based testing framework Cucumber use Gherkin language to write specifications. Although, there are some standard rules of Given, When, Then, And are supposed to be followed. For further analysis of test smells in this project, we will consider Gauge framework as a case study, which is quite famous and young testing framework. All of the test smell definitions used in this article, are taken from a systematic mapping study of test smell detection tools .

heading: Objectives
content: The main focus area of the project deals with the NLP based mapping of BDD specification for detection of test smells in test cases. To this end, we shall: To collect a curated dataset of BDD specifications for empirical analysis. To develop an NLP-based system for mapping BDD specifications to test code. To introduce an approach for detecting test smells at the specification level. To introduce the mechanism that detect the mapping smells from specifications to implementation. To analyze the result and compare with the state-of-the-art tools that detect smells.

heading: Related Work
content: The related work is mainly focused on the systematic literature reviews over the past few years, and it has shown that TDD and BDD has been widely used and researched. Many researcher promote the adoption of BDD based testing because of its effectiveness and support for business modeling people involved in the system testing. It is widely known that test smells negatively affect the program code quality , and therefore many studies have been proposed to automatically identify and remove test smells from the test cases especially at source code level . But there are very less studies found that draw an attention towards test smells considerations at BDD specification level. Islam et al.  claims that the BDD is lacking of standard methods and techniques for identifying and Refactoring the test smells. Binamungu et al.  wrote a thesis on detecting the duplication’s of specification from the BDD frameworks. In his thesis he proposed a framework that detects duplicate scenarios from the specification based on the comparison of its characteristics, that were extracted from the scenario executions. His main focus was on production patterns used by each scenario, and consider the other (duplicate) scenario as a smell if it has the same execution functionality. The author Causevic et al.  highlighted that several experienced developers took comparatively very less time to finish test driven task than the in comparison with a new user. However, for an inexperienced person it would be fast to write BDD based testing specifications. The benefit of using BDD based testing lies when the team collaborate, allowing everyone in the team representing to write test cases for system under test. Abushama et al.  have examined several important aspects of BDD vs TDD regrading their success rate by considering different factors, i.e., cost, time, and quality, which shows the customer satisfaction. heading: Abstract
content: Neurodevelopmental conditions are the ones that impact the cognitive abilities of a person. The causes of such conditions are not known but genetics can be considered to have a major impact. Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is also a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects the behavioral activities of a person. The people having this condition are characterized by difficulties in social interaction and they also face challenges in learning and linguistic competence. With early diagnoses and targeted behavioral practices, such a condition can be improved significantly, positively impacting one’s life. Machine learning and deep learning have introduced intelligent systems which have revolutionized the traditional clinical diagnosis approaches which are costly and time-consuming as compared to the complementary diagnosis systems.  Considering ASD, in the traditional diagnoses setting, psychiatrists or psychologists conduct interviews with the parents which are followed by prolonged behavioral observations. This becomes troublesome for both patients and their guardians. To address these concerns, this project aims to streamline the ASD detection process by utilizing the most crucial behavioral traits that contribute to the ASD classification in the early stages of a child’s life. Q-CHAT-10 and AQ-10 datasets will be used to train the predictive models. These datasets contain behavioral questions that are related to a child social interaction. Various ML and DL algorithms like Support Vector Machines (SVM), Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Networks and Gradient Boosting Machines etc. will be employed on the behavioral traits that are tailored for toddlers and adolescents. A comprehensive evaluation of these algorithms will be performed by using evaluation methods like Cross-Validation, Precision-Recall Curve, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve and Area Under the Curve (AUC) etc.  The trained model will then be integrated into a mobile application. The outcome will be a mobile application that would help the children navigating the challenges of ASD, by early diagnoses of the condition which have proven to produce better social outcomes in the person’s life due to the appropriateness of therapy and treatment.

heading: Introduction
content: Some neurodevelopment disorders are not completely curable, but timely treatment can have a profound impact on the quality of one’s life and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is one of them. It influences the social interactions and learning capabilities in a person’s life. Empirical studies have proven that ASD cannot be diagnosed with a straightforward clinical test . There are varying degrees of severity and symptoms for autism which makes it a broad-spectrum disorder. The symptoms often overlap with other neurodevelopment disorders which makes the diagnosis process a complex task. Several behavioral tests are used in the diagnosis process of ASD. Some of these include Q-CHAT (Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers) , DISCO (Diagnostic Interview for Social and Communication Disorders) , and ADOS (Autism Diagnostic observation Schedule) . These behavioral tests come with a set of challenges, for example, ADOS may not be suitable for non-verbal adolescents. Moreover, trained professionals are required for the administration of these tests. Furthermore, the tests are lengthy and costly. Consequently, conventional diagnostic systems underscore the need for a system that can facilitate early diagnosis of ASD and enable the healthcare providers to recommend appropriate treatment. The automatic diagnosis of ASD at an early stage will improve the adaptive skills of a person and will provide adult independence. The advent of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques has significantly enhanced clinical methodologies . However, the main challenge in developing an automatic ASD detection system using ML and DL techniques is the availability of adequate data of high quality. A child’s behavioral data is difficult to record and when it comes to a neurodevelopment disorder, parents or guardians hesitate to share such information. Moreover, recording a child’s behavior demands patience and it raises privacy concerns as well. To solve this problem, this project aims to leverage state-of-the-art ML and DL techniques for classifying ASD or Non-ASD cases. Additionally, we will identify the traits that significantly influence the technique's outcomes by utilizing datasets like Q-Chat-10 and AQ-10 . These benchmark datasets are most widely used for studying ASD. Furthermore, the analysis will extend to the attributes/traits of toddlers and children, exploring their associations with ASD. By comparing the results of various techniques, our goal is to determine the most effective method across all datasets. Towards the project's conclusion, efforts will be made to integrate ASD data from Pakistani children, if available, thereby contributing to a more comprehensive understanding of ASD across diverse populations. We believe the proposed solution will assist parents and healthcare professionals by providing timely ASD diagnoses and enable them to start potential treatment.

heading: Related Work
content: ASD is a neuro-developmental condition that impacts social interaction, communication, and behavior, necessitating early identification for a productive intervention. It has been reported that in the United States alone, 1 out of 54 children are affected by Autism. Many studies have been published regarding the application of various ML and DL techniques which promise various aspects for enhancing accuracy and efficiency in ASD task. Ahmed Hadri  utilized a hybrid approach by combining machine learning models, SVM and Random Forest, with questionnaires to improve accuracy. The dataset was collected locally using various screening tools i.e. AQ-10, CBCL etc. An accuracy of 97.5% was achieved through the used methodology, indicating promising results for early ASD detection. Maitha  employed machine learning algorithms (XgBoost, Naïve Bayes etc.) to predict specific ASD symptoms in individuals and determine the optimal model for diagnosis. The data was based upon the AQ-10 screening tool and was collected via a mobile application. The dataset contains 1811 attributes after preprocessing. The analysis of the dataset reveals that the toddler age groups contribute the most data, with approximately 70% diagnosed with ASD. Muhammad Shoaib  applied federated learning with logistic regression and Support Vector Machine for ASD detection. Datasets were collected from Kaggle including Autism image dataset for children and Autism Screening on Adults. FL technique achieved an accuracy of 98% in children and 81% in adults for Autism detection. Dipti  used Machine Learning approaches (Random Forest, SVM) on a questionnaire model M-Chat; however, the dataset used is not specified by the author. Random forest showed better accuracy of 86% compared to SVM, contributing to an automated autism detection system. Gennaro  applied ML algorithms: Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression and K-nearest neighbors to investigate the Q-Chat for autism screening. The ML achieved an accuracy of 90% overall, with SVM being the most effective at 95%. H. Abbas  trained in two algorithms using structured parent-reported questionnaires and key behaviors from home videos. Feature selection, engineering and encoding techniques were applied to handle data challenges. Clinical data from thousands of at-risk children for Autism were included in the dataset. As a result, significant improvement in screening accuracy compared to standard tools was demonstrated through metrics such as AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. The SHIFO AI team  developed the Autizm AI application available on Apple AppStore. The model used in the application is trained on collected data of over 1,054 children. The data is based on the behavioral questions listed by the Q-Chat screening tool. This model allows the user to predict the presence or absence of ASD with 97% accuracy. Similarly, an application named ASDetect  developed at La Trobe University is available on the Google Playstore. This app enables parents and practitioners to review early possible signs of Autism in childhood. With actual clinical videos of children with and without ASD, each question focuses on specific social communication behavior i.e. pointing or social smiling. Concludingly, the above listed studies have employed various ML and DL techniques for ASD detection, have contributed largely to advancing the field. However, these techniques come with certain drawbacks, i.e., time-consuming, resource-expensive, and financially burdensome. Studies that involve behavioral, facial expression, structural emotional, mental disorder analysis, and medical imagery often demand huge time and financial investments. These techniques may showcase promise in accuracy and efficiency, but their implementation could be impractical for widespread adoption due to costs and resource requirements.

heading: Methodology
content: The datasets that will be used include Q-CHAT-10 (Quantitative checklist for Autism in Toddlers) dataset and AQ-10-child (Autism Spectrum Quotient) dataset. Q-CHAT-10 dataset contains 10 behavioral questions data for toddlers. There is total 1054 instances with 18 attributes.  AQ-10 child dataset contains 10 behavioral questions for children of the age 4-11. There is a total of 292 instances with 21 features. The project will follow agile methodology by training a predictive model and integrating it into a mobile application. The App and the model will be improved as the project progresses. Initially, the behavioral data will be explored, and EDA (exploratory data analysis) will be applied to it. This will be followed by feature engineering to find the traits that can be used as input for the model. Various ML and DL techniques will be applied to the data and the resulting models will be evaluated. After evaluation, the models will be cross compared to identify the most accurate one. The data will be analyzed to find out the connections between behavioral traits and ASD by using statistical methods. heading: Problem Statement
content: The three key challenges faced by Pakistan's farmers are: (1) inability to get timely localized agriculture information, such as government programs, crop calendars, and disease management strategies, (2) literacy and connectivity issues since most farmers are illiterate or semi-literate and inhabit regions with weak internet connectivity, and (3) reliance on unscientific agriculture practices, wherein irrigation and use of fertilizers are done on a guesswork basis without any scientific inputs. There are currently existing mobile applications and SMS platforms that have tried to solve some of these problems, but none of these solutions have offline capabilities, real-time weather forecasting, or connectivity with low-cost IoT devices. In view of, a complete, focused on farmers solution is urgently needed. Farmers in Pakistan lack localized information, are illiterate, have connectivity issues, and have no access to intelligent, mostly offline, sensors (IoT) based decision support system DSS.

heading: Proposed Solution
content: To address these problems, this project proposes PAKFASAL, a mobile application developed in Flutter that provides agricultural education and decision support in a farmer-centric manner. The app will deliver tutorials, articles, and videos in multiple local languages, ensuring accessibility for farmers across Pakistan. A voice-to-text interface will allow illiterate farmers to interact with the app naturally, while offline caching will make content available even in low-connectivity regions. The system integrates real-time weather forecasting and IoT-based soil sensors (pH and moisture), offering actionable insights on irrigation scheduling and fertilizer usage. In addition, the app will feature a farmer–company marketplace to eliminate middlemen and a query portal where farmers can upload crop issues (text, voice, or pictures) for expert or AI-driven responses.

heading: Problem Statement
content: Farmers in Pakistan face a range of interrelated hurdles that highly impede agricultural productivity and sustainability. The first hurdle relates to the relatively timely and localized agricultural information informing such as government support programs, crop calendars, and disease/pest management practices. Farmers therefore cannot make informed choices without such information sources. The second hurdle relates to the many illiteracy and connectivity challenges. Many farmers are illiterate or semi-illiterate and live in rural locations where connectivity is the most inadequate. This blocks those individuals from using digital tools or accessing newer knowledge of practices and innovations. Additionally, many farmers remain committed to using traditional or un-scientific practices and often make decisions around irrigation, fertilizer and pest management from instinct instead of from supporting data or information. While some mobile apps or SMS applications exist to challenge some of these issues, little exists to provide offline tools or real-time weather forecasts or connect with cost-sensitive IoT devices. In this context, we need to produce a solution that is holistic, farmer-centred and that could be used, even in low-connectivity situations, to build on intelligent decision support systems (DSS) based on sensors.

heading: Objectives
content: The overall goal of the PAKFASAL project is the creation of an intelligent farm platform that will supply location-based precise recommendations to the farmer with an integrated Suggestion System and Decision Support System (DSS).The platform is designed to support famers at making decisions on which crops to use, time of planting, irrigation scheduling, and disease management by processing real-time information on current weather and soil conditions and local farming practices. PAKFASAL distinguishes itself from other static sources of information by creating customized and personalized recommendations that address specific locations and requirements of each farmer, helping them be highly productive and take minimal risks. By its decision support functionality, the system enables famers to embrace sustainability, optimize use of sources, and overall increase efficiency in farm operations, which leads directly to enhanced crop output and agricultural development within Pakistan.

heading: Related Work
content: In the last few years, there has been an interest in using Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in agriculture to assist farmers in decision-making and management of resources. Some mobile applications and IoT solutions have been created globally, but most of them have not been localized, supported offline, or made accessible for illiterate farmers. One major category of related work is mobile-based agricultural advisory systems.

heading: Abstract
content: Nexkey Project is to develop an android keyboard capable of identifying frequently used words to provide personalized and improved typing experience using its prediction system that would use Android API to implement a keyboard with elastic layout that would modify the selected key which is predicted to be clicked next and the victim key which is predicted to not be clicked in case of the word that is being typed by giving selected key more width and reducing the width of victim key. The application will always look for the  victim key from keys which are on either side of the selected key. This app will provide an alternative to already available keyboards on the app store which provides suggestion on-screen which for some people is rather annoying. This will result in user typing their messages at high speed without needing to glance at their keyboards and will reduce the use of backspace key. heading: Introduction
content: Smartphones have quickly become the most important gadgets of our life and provided us with many features that use to require laptop and desktop syst ems. Every year  cell phone industry is progressing towards larger and better displays on their devices by reducing the size of bezels hoping to provide users with distraction free interaction with their device. This means there is no place for physical keyboards instead virtual keyboards are the future. Our Final year project is to develop an Android Keyboard App that will help in avoiding or reducing the mistyping of words due to speedy typing or accidently pressing the key right next to the correct key. Like other available smart keyboards this keyboard will also create a database of words but instead of giving suggestions above the keyboard this app will suggest and predict the next alphabet the user is going to type from previous usage of words thus predicting next alphabet. The app will work in a way that when user clicks an alphabet, it will predict the next alphabet that would be used on the basis of the recently pressed alphabet key and the previously used words that had those same alphabets in same order. As soon as an alphabet key is pressed, the next suggested key will be twice regular key width as one of its neighbour would be selected as a victim key . As user continues to type the word every next alphabet will more specific to the word that is bei ng typed In this way, the user keeps pressing the keys and it will keeps suggesting the next alphabet key leading to the word the user wanted to type. Keyboard will assist user typing by changing the colour of the key as well as increasing its width . Keyboard will also provide the word that is most likely being typed in space bar so user is not forced to type long words completely. Other than users personalized words database would also contain most frequently used stop words in English language. Although these keyboards are quite popular these days many users still don’t prefer autocorrect feature as this feature itself can cause mistakes due to misinterpretation of the word being typed. There are also users th at tend to turn suggestion off on their keyboards. We aim to create an app that facilitate users by speeding up their typing and reducing mistypes without forcing any suggestions on screen or modifying already typed words.

heading: Scope

heading: Abstract
content: With the growth of  internet, the world is shifting towards smart buildings and automated systems, which not only reduces effort to control household appliances but is also energy efficient and time saver. A significant concern related to IOT based devices is security. The basic challenge in the IOT based home security and automation i s providing a control to the user over  internet as it is less secure than Ethernet or Bluetooth connectivity.  In order to address this issue, we developed a CASA CONSOLE system w hich provides a complete home automation at one point with enough efficiency a nd total control of appliances with  the monitoring system . The architecture is designed in such a way that a user not only holds the ownership of device but also the data involved related to the user. heading: Motivation
content: Our work is greatly inspired by the CASA Jasmina project.  The project  has been nominated for 21 projects in the ACADEMY AWARDS and won the ED ITORS CHOICE award IOT 2015/16[8 ]. In the project, the team maintained an apartment totally based on IOT and declared it as an open source project to let people work on the sensors installed in that apartment. They provided an integrated IOT system for home automation and allow the developers to contribute. [9]. The motivation is to build the system which is not only one point complete home automation but must be secure enough to implement it even at sensitive places such as banks. To achieve that we have studied the multiple cryptographic algorithms that can be implemented on open communica tion between client, server, compared them, and propose the solution which is best for the system. CASA CONSOLE is to provide the one point home controller for all the appliances installed in the house. The system not only provides the complete control but ensures the ownership of the user by providing the data including history of actions performed on the system and the user related information on the microcontroller which is owned by the client and present inside the home of the client.  Furthermore the communication between the end points is encrypted with strong encryption algorithm AES which makes it secure enough to implement the system on security critical buildings as well.

heading: Introduction
content: In every local organization, tracking of employees work, performance and their attendance on daily basis is a general and an important task for the betterment of an organization. Because it helps an organization to make important decisions like promotion, devotion and suspension of employees, moreover it also helps them to make salaries as per the work done by the employees. The purpose of this project “smart incident report” is to track employees work and generate their daily, weekly, monthly and annually basis performance reports by analysing their work hours, their arrival and departure time from the work field and their attendance. Moreover it also generate employee’s salaries by analysing their working hours on daily basis, and can perform actions of deduction and add bonus on salaries as per organization defined criteria. A web app that will provides local organizations, industries, offices, banks to track their employee’s performance and generate their daily, weekly, monthly and annual basis reports by keeping in view of their performance and working hours, which help organizations to become efficient, boost their work and help them to minimize the man force which they had hired to mark  attendance, keeping record of employees arrival and departure from the work field and generate hand written reports which is time consuming and less efficient. So, it is very mandatory to develop such system that can help organizations and high authoriti Ses of them to find and differentiate the lazy and faineant employees from the workforce, which helps to make organization resources optimize and efficient.

heading: Objectives
content: The main objective of this system is to track and analyse the employees performance within a local organization, and generate reports on daily, weekly, monthly and annually basis by keeping in view of their working hours and their performance. heading: Implementation
content: We have created ontologies using the symmetric approach  [4]. The focus of our project revolves around the merging and mapping of ontologies, there are tools to perform this task but we are manually merging and mapping the concepts. Ontology merging, as its name implies, merges the concepts that match semantically with each other into a single concept. In the symmetric approach, data of the ontologies is fetched via SPARQL  query, and the query merges the data of both the ontologies, resulting in merging of ontologies. The web and android interfaces ar e designed to facilitate the user in viewing and purchasing different products. The interface will allow the user to register their profiles and login the application. Ontologies are created in protégé which does not allow every SPARQL query to be processed. SPARQL queries are used to process the RDF datasets, for this purpose we devised a solution in Jena Fuseki[5], which process the range of SPARQL queries to fulfil our requirements. We researched and then developed SPARQL queries to perform the required functionalities. To connect J ena Fuseki server datasets with web, we have built a new API which will receive and send requests to connect web with Fuseki server and with android. Fuseki server cannot work alone. To solve this problem, we used Ubuntu linode server so we can upload fuseki on linode. We used linode to get data on web server which will be connected to web easily. API will send and receive requests to web server and then server will send JSON[6] data to android. OWL ontology is built by following steps:  Create the classes, subclasses and provide information about them. All the classes will be subclass of owl:Thing.  Create data properties and provide Domain which will be the class in the ontology. Enter range of the data property which will be the int, double or string. All the data properties will be the subclass of owl: topDataProperty.

heading: Abstract
content: This project aims to develop an intelligent vehicle assistance and safety system by integrating advanced technologies across multiple domains. The primary objectives include real-time object detection and frame annotation using YOLOv8, facilitating obstacle and hazard identification, and enhancing driver awareness through annotated video frames with bounding boxes, labels, distance estimates, and safety warnings. An automatic braking system uses additional sensors and image processing to reduce opposite collision risk. Automatic wiper activation, as well as rain detection, are considered to utilize rain sensors that are interfaced to an Arduino microcontroller so that visibility is clear during bad weather conditions. The proposed system is a fingerprint- based security system for biometric vehicle access, along with IoT enabled GPS monitoring to increase security by way of real time alerts and access logs. IR and ultrasonic sensors are employed by blind spot detection and parking assistance systems to enhance safety during such moves in limited space. Moreover, conceptual research is inherited to attempt to improve the speed and energy efficiency of solar powered vehicles with provided insights and the suggestions. Together, these innovations seek to make for a safer, more efficient and technologically superior way of driving. Table of Contents

heading: Introduction
content: Solar powered cars are fast becoming the revolutionary concept in transportation, largely thanks to the growing demand for sustainable and eco-friendly solutions in transportation. These cars take the benefit of renewable solar energy to help diminish fossil fuel dependence and greenhouse gas emission. Yet, solar powered cars aren’t yet widespread because they confront several challenges. The problem of this project is related to these challenges, which can be minimized by integrating image processing and Internet of Things (IoT) into solar powered cars, which would improve them in functionality, efficiency and user experience. This project  provide the most ideal performance of solar powered vehicles as long as they are practical and easy to be utilized. Using image processing, the car achieves more advanced safety features than what is available today such as obstacle detection which also increases road safety by allowing autonomous breakage. The second advantage is that IoT based systems provide vehicle security systems as well as a user-friendly interface. Road safety is one of the most important global issues, as evidenced by the startling data that almost 5 million vehicle accidents occur each year and result in about 1.3 million fatalities globally. The majority of human mistakes and negligence including distracted driving, and disregard for fundamental safety precautions. Conventional cars, which depend entirely on human control and attention while in motion, frequently serve as the unfortunate setting for accidents in which human error is a major contributing factor. Overall, vehicle conditions, untrained driving, and drowsy driving contribute to the share of road accident involvement. This project focuses on innovation, implementing systems on state-of-the-art technologies to solve real world problems. Another core system developed is object detection and frame annotation using the state-of-the-art computer vision model YOLOv8. This system takes raw video frames, and in real time is capable of detecting and annotating objects, outputting bounding boxes, labels, distance estimates, and safety warnings. This is a great road safety feature because it alerts the driver of what to stay out. The project is also critical to the integration of a rain detection system using rain sensor, Arduino microcontroller automatically activating wipers. It guarantees optimal visibility under adverse weather conditions and make it more convenient and safer. The system is made with fingerprint dependent unlocking systems coupled with an IoT enabled monitoring platform for security. With this system, not only is it ensured that only authorized users can access the vehicle, but should an invalid fingerprint attempt be made to use the vehicle, receive GPS location alerts as well. In addition, the vehicle comes with a blind spot alarming system and parking distance warning system. Infrared and ultrasonic sensors detect obstacles in the car’s blind spots and in proximity and provide real-time alerts to the driver to avoid collision. Finally, the project contains a detailed report on how strategies can help in increasing the speed and efficiency of solar powered vehicles so future research and development in this area can be laid down. This project shows how renewable energy combined with advanced technologies can be used to help address critical sustainable transportation challenges. This work integrates safety, security and energy efficiency features onto a solar powered vehicle and contributes to the creation of smarter, safer and a sustainable mobility solution. This report will enable readers to look at the different ways that these enhancements can make the ride safer, more energy efficient and more interactive with users. Ultimately this project hopes to create a more sustainable and interconnected future in the field of transportation.

heading: Background
content: Since the addition of renewable energy and advance automation technology, the global transportation sector is experiencing a transformation. Solar-powered vehicles currently possess the potential to play a role in providing a sustainable means of decreasing the greenhouse gases produced by vehicles while dealing with the rising energy demands of the future. More than this, modern vehicles are combining features for safety and convenience that are intelligent and powered by IoT, machine learning and microcontroller systems. It consists of this review of latest developments in solar powered vehicle along with fingerprint door locking system, door fingerprint security system, GPS module for real time tracking and servo motors based automatic rain wipers. Microcontrollers like Arduino and ESP have a pivotal role in achieving all these functionalities which include processing sensor data, image recognition and so on and actuation. In addition, autonomous braking systems present a major step forward from typical sensor-based approach to systems based on image processing and computer vision. Though these modern approaches revolutionize efficiency and reliability, sensors remain indispensable in everything from rain detection to blind spot monitoring, and to so many other important systems. This review is extended further to include automatic rain wipers that are provided using servo motors that dynamically respond to precipitation in order to provide greater driver safety and comfort. In this review, we analyze the evolution of these technologies and their combined effects on vehicle automation together to illuminate research gaps and opportunities for future advances.

heading: Conclusion
content: The creation of this project shows a thorough strategy for improving vehicle security, driver support, and road safety while fostering accessibility and cost. In order to ensure driver awareness and obstacle avoidance, the project reaches a major milestone by using state-of-the-art technologies like YOLOv8 for real-time object identification and frame annotation. This is further enhanced by the automated braking system, which uses sensor integration and image processing methods to proactively avoid crashes. By automating wiper controls to lessen driver workload and increase safety, the rain detection and automatic wiper activation module tackles vision issues during inclement weather. In addition to offering real-time location alerts for improved vehicle security, the fingerprint-based security system with IoT GPS monitoring adds  biometric verification to prevent unwanted access. By employing infrared and ultrasonic sensors to identify obstructions and alert drivers, blind spot detection and parking assistance systems improve situational awareness in situations that are typically difficult. These characteristics enable drivers to confidently maneuver through confined spaces and steer clear of possible hazards. In order to maximize the speed and energy efficiency of solar-powered cars, the project also involves conceptual research, which will provide important information for future sustainable transportation options. All things considered, this project effectively combines cutting-edge technologies with useful applications, accomplishing its goals of efficiency, security, and safety. It bridges the gap between high-end automotive advances and mass-market accessibility thanks to its modular construction, cost-effective components, and scalable design. This work lays the groundwork for future developments in the sector and marks a major advancement in intelligent vehicle safety systems.

heading: Implementation
content: In this current chapter, we outline the design and implementation of an independent vehicle assistance and safety platform and focus on both the implementation of individual operational modules and the coordination of the discrete modules in a central control execution. Data acquisition, decision-making, and real-time execution are based on the concurrent processing of the principal core, which is a Raspberry Pi 4. The individual modules such as object detection, rain sensing, RFID based vehicle access and blind-spot monitoring are assembled using a home-built printed circuit board which sort out the signals detrostitution and supply power in a military-like organization. The object detection system modelled with the help of the YOLOv8 deep -learning model en ables the vehicle to detect and classify the nearby objects located, including pedestrians, other vehicles, and motionless obstacles. Digested information triggers the implementation of appropriately suitable actions, including automatic braking provisions  to the visual exhibition of the warnings. Raspberry Pi is a central communicator device among other peripheral/slave modules whose connection is coordinated through the modular architecture integrating the I 2 C, UART, and GPIO protocols depending on the properties of the given sensor/device in question. Specifically, infrared sensors used to detect a blind- spot are connected through GPIO pins, but RFID readers and significant rain-detection module use a UART or digital pin-based signalling. The scalable integration is made possible with this modular scheme and the debugging process of developing the hardware becomes easier. Its power supply is designed to both conserve energy and reliably be able to provide a consistent energy source where an energy supp ly that uses voltage change is the direct -current (DC) battery. The voltage regulation is also guaranteed using buck converters, which produce steady 5 V and 3.3 V output used by the Raspberry Pi and other parts. heading: Problem Statement
content: The purpose of designing such platform is that patients are unable to provide their complete medical history such as prescriptions, test reports and the details of the doctors who diagnose their disease previously. Due to which doctors find it difficult to correctly diagnose the disease of the patient in a better way because they do not know their previous medical history. Moreover, the busy schedule of doctors needs this type of system, which assists them in diagnosing disease of the patient in a modernized and calculated way. In order to resolve this issue we provide a solution in the form of an online health care system that will assist doctor in diagnosing the disease of the patient. Because we store symptoms of 40 to 50 commonly occurring diseases using machine learning approach that will assist doctor to diagnose the disease of the patient. In addition to that, doctor can view previous medical history of the patient such as prescriptions and their dosage, prescribes test and their reports and the details of the doctor who diagnose the patient previously without any ambiguity or redundancy in the data. Retrieving of data without any redundancy is because doctor will use the patient CNIC no in order to view the patient previous medications and obviously every patient has unique CNIC No against their previous medical history, so there will be zero chance of data redundancy.

heading: Scope
content: This project is designed to maintain the medical records of patients along with details of their respective doctors. There are many areas around the globe where there is a lack of such automated system. The system assists doctor to diagnose the disease of the patient in a calculated way using machine learning approach. The system provides many services for patients, which includes; daily treatments, registration of patients, maintain records for patient’s medical history, search best hospitals or doctors according to their needs within few seconds respectively. This system contains:  Login and registration forms for (patients, doctors, receptionists, pharmacist, laboratory and hospitals)  The system shall allow (patients, doctors, receptionists, pharmacist, laboratory and hospitals) to edit their information like name, contact number, address, etc as identified in the introduction of the report. The following languages used within the system to enable development and implementation: PhpMyAdmin is used for keeping records about all the registered members of the system for security, accuracy and reliability each patient record shall kept against their CNIC number (backside we use SQL Server for databases development). Server side scripting shall do with java, php, embedded in html and java web server will facilitate simultaneous processing. This system is implemented using the languages PHP, HTML, CSS, BOOTSTRAP, Javasrcipt, Laravel framework, and SQL server management for databases and PhpMyAdmin only. We are not using any other programming language for the implementation purposes like Java, C sharp etc. It’s a complete web based application implemented by web-based components. Other than that we are not providing any rating feature to all the doctors because it might possible that the doctor which has more experience than other doctors have the lowest rating in the system as compared to the doctor who have less experience because of patients reviews.

content: For testing purposes we use unit testing approach, we test each functionality at the en d of its implementation so that if the functionality required any changes it can be implemented as early as possible. Other than that we test each module as well when it is completely developed i n order to verify that all the functionalities are successfully implemented and are accordi ng to customer needs and expectations. We use unit testing approach due to the following advantages:  Unit testing increases confidence in changing/maintaining code.  Codes are more reusable when unit testing approach is used in the development of application  The cost of fixing a bug/defect during unit testing is lesser in comparison to  that of defects detected at higher levels.  Debugging is easy. When the test fails only the latest changes made to the functi onality needs to be debugged.

heading: Abstract
content: Color plays a crucial role in our perception and interaction with the world, en- hancing object visualization and recognition. This project aims to revolutionize color mixing technology by automating the process with precision and accuracy. Leveraging image processing techniques and IoT (Internet of Things) technology, the system identifies colors in real-time and adjusts the ratio of primary colors to achieve the desired shade. The project begins with an exploration of various color models, including RGB (Red, Green, Blue) and CMYK (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black), elucidating their significance in digital displays and printing applications. It then delves into the HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color model, crucial for color detection in the pro- posed system. The core of the system lies in its ability to convert input images into the HSV color space and analyze the Hue component to identify colors accurately. Commands are sent to an Arduino microcontroller based on color detection, enabling precise manipulation of an industrial robot for pick and place tasks. Real-time monitoring and control are facilitated through IoT integration, optimizing resource utilization and minimizing waste. The project addresses challenges in traditional color production methods, offer- ing a solution that streamlines the process, reduces human error, and enhances efficiency. Through algorithm development, sensor integration, and user-friendly interface design, the system aims to set a new standard in automated color recog- nition and mixing technology. iii Table of content: Color is the fundamental aspect of our perception and interaction with the world. Color improves the visualization and recognition of an object. These colors are the shades of three basic primary colors Red, Green, and blue. Different Color models mix these colors in a specific ratio to make various shades. A few Color models are RGB, CMYK, and HSV . The basic purpose of this machine is to improve the color mixing technology to form these shades with precision and accuracy. It uses image processing techniques to recognize the color and then applies different algorithms to set the ratio of each primary color to form the required shade.

heading: Problem Statement
content: In traditional color production, colors are created by manually mixing primary colors in specific ratios based on color codes. However, this manual process is prone to human error and sometimes results in incorrect proportions. Additionally, there may be instances where the ratio of a particular color component exceeds the desired amount. Hence, there is a need to develop an automatic machine that minimizes human effort to proceed with the process of color production.

heading: Literature Review
content: Since the early 1970s, color has played a pivotal role in our daily lives. However, during that era, the process of obtaining colors was laborious, requiring manual mixing of primary colors. This process causes many errors [7]. To streamline the resultant color in production, we embarked on an extensive research journey, exploring diverse methodologies. This comprehensive review has unveiled several promising avenues for automating color production. Our project comprises two primary components: image processing and color mixing using primary colors. In this literature review, we will delve into various techniques and strategies aimed at realizing the automation of this machine.

heading: Introduction
content: In this chapter,we explains the integration of a mobile application developed in Flutter with a backend image processing server (computer) built using Flask. The main objective of this integration is to allow users to capture or select an image through the app or select to the gallery then send it to the server and receive the extracted CMYK and white color values . This function is very critical for automacally color detection process in our pigment mixing mechine, almost show accurate color analysis and real-time processing. The system uses modern technologies such as Flutter for the frontend interface, Flask (Python) for the backend server, and OpenCV for image filtering and K clustering. The communication between the app and server is established through REST API calls(is use for communication and data exchange between difference system). This architecture not only enables real-time interaction between mobile and server but also ensures modularity, ease of testing of the project.

heading: Results
content: Initially, a green-colored image was selected from the gallery and uploaded for processing. After a short delay, the server responded with the extracted CMYK values: Cyan = 56.6, Magenta = 0, Yellow = 54.29, and Black = 31.37. These values were then sent to the ESP32 microcontroller. The ESP32 first calculated and displayed the required volume (in milliliters) of each CMYK and White pig- ment needed to reproduce the target color. Following this, the motors for each respective pigment were activated one by one to dispense the exact quantities.

heading: Abstract
content: Software Defined Networks (SDN) is the latest technology and it is still in progress. In other Countries, SDN is being implemented in different organization. In Pakistan, however we are still just learning about this concept. This will solve many physical and other problems related to networking. In this final year project, we aim to design a SDN Network for COMSATS’s different campuses. First of all, we will make a COMSATS’s network of two or more than two campuses and then we will generate security threats like DDoS attacks. After generating the attacks, we will first study the attack patterns and then generate some prevention scheme for blocking the attacks.

heading: Problem Statement
content: With the increasing network scale and requirements in computer networking many problems occur. Some of these problems include, delays and lack of reliability in communication, poor network management, low robustness and less flexibility. Keeping in mind the end goal to adapt to these issues, SDN proposed another system engineering to manage these issues. In SDN, flow installations at switches is a complex mechanism. In this project, we will learn SDN and its working. In addition, w e will implement different flow installation mechanisms, different modified  algorithms to optimize network in terms of bandwidth and latency and deploying firewall in the controller to secure the network analyzed the performance of these parameters.

heading: Introduction
content: Software-defined networking (SDN) is a term in which we can make our network more flexible as compared to our traditional networks. The SDN help us to respond quickly to changing business requirements. Software Defined Networking provided us an approach in building, designing and managing network. It enables us to separate forwarding plane and control plane. Also, it provides us the ability to directly program the network thus giving us an impression of underlying structure for network services and application. In SDN, we can change the flow of traffic without touching the switch and routers of network. Now, the question is why SDN still not implemented in Lahore or Pakistan? Because our infrastructure is not ready yet for SDN technology because if we use SDN then we have to change our hardware and software as well which is not possible or it costs too much. Also, our organizations still not ready for this and also because of insufficient SDN support skills. In this final year project, we aim to design an SDN Network for COMSATS’s different campuses. First of all, we will make a COMSATS’s network of two or more than two campuses and then we will generate security threats like DDoS attacks. DDoS is short for Di stributed Denial of Service.  DDoS is a type of DOS attack where multiple compromised systems, which are often infected with a Trojan, are used to target a single system causing a Denial of Service (DoS)  attack. After generating the attacks, we will first s tudy the attack patterns and then generate some prevention scheme for blocking the attacks. We have proposed a new algorithm for prevention of DDOS attack. We will be identifying user types. It will detect if a user is an attacker or not. If the user is attacker, then we block it else it is allowed access.

heading: Methodology
content: The flow installation mechanisms are an important part of running SDN as new flows are installed as per network requirements with the passage of time. We have implemented these flow installation mechanisms via POX controller and Mininet Emulator.  Moreover, we used Virtual Box along with Ubuntu Operating System which runs OpenFlow as the simulator and compatible with Mininet. In addition, we used windows Operating system and Ubuntu Opera ting system for the analysis and implementation of our research work. For this purpose, we created different network topologies along with their virtual hosts, routers, switches, and SDN controller. After creating topologies, we installed flows followed by three approaches reactive, proactive and hybrid. We analyzed these approaches with the help of Mininet Emulator.

There is delay in the throughput of traditional network as compared to SDN network.

heading: Abstract
content: Report elaborates the project where the analysis of user behaviour is done with the help of social data mining approach. Our goal is to see how the data on social media sites can enable us to create a pattern of events and the behaviour a user exhibits. The data is extracted from social sites such as Twitter using a web scraper and stored in databases. That data is processed through many steps i.e. data cleaning, data classification, sentimental analysis and visualization. In data cleaning phase, unwanted data is cleaned through different cleaning techniques. Then data is classified for analysis. Then sentimental analysis is performed a ccording to negative and positive remarks. The results of sentimental analysis are then visualized in the form of graphs. At last, a web front end is used where all phases are integrated to provide ease in use to the users. Different data mining algorithms are used to identify the patterns to analyse the data. Brief history events are elaborated to show the difference present in the previous development and that provided by the project. More over, project defines a new era where the ease for studying behaviour using huge data without surveys takes place.

heading: Abstract
content: Diabetes is a very common disease which refers to insufficient production (Type 1 Diabetes) or mismanagement (Type 2 Diabetes) of insulin by the body. Over the years, there has been a drastic increase in the number o f diabetics globally. From 108 million in 1980, the number has risen to 422 million as of 2014. Diabetes causes severe problems such as lower limb amputation, heart attacks, stroke, kidney failure and blindness. Unfortunately, many diabetics do not realiz e the gravity of their disease or fail to acquire sufficient knowledge and succumb to horrendous consequences. Before we even begin to highlight the ways in which diabetes is countered, it is essential to spread awareness among diabetics and educate them about diabetes. As researchers try their best to find a permanent cure, the only viable solution available to date is managing and controlling body vitals regularly to avoid complications caused by diabetes. Diabetics need to keep daily, weekly and yearly track of their blood glucose levels, insulin levels, blood pressure, cholesterol, carbohydrates and exercise routines. If these vitals are not managed, it may cause damage to vessels supplying blood to important organs. Therefore, diabetes should be taken very seriously. Traditionally, diabetics have used diaries to log their readings which has turned out to be a very inconvenient and tedious activity. MedShare is a web application that makes the lives of diabetics much easier. Not only does it aim at improv ing the way in which medical readings are logged, it provides additional tools such as diabetes unit convertors and calculators. It provides detailed infographics and charts spanning over different time spans showing an overview of the readings. These logged readings can also be shared among others, especially doctors, within MedShare, by e-mail and on social media platforms such as Facebook. Diabetics are provided with a social platform including blogs and forums within MedShare where they can communicate with other members and doctors as well. They can read others’ blogs and also write personal blogs to raise awareness and other issues in the community, providing a better chance of getting relevant and informed responses.

heading: Architecture
content: For this project we are using Laravel PHP Framework which follows the MVC structure. Figure 9 software architecture diagram It comprises of three major components; Controller, Model and View. The controller manages the Http requests, using the model to load any necessary data from the database and passing it onto the view. The view usually consists of HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Users only interact with the view to achieve their objectives. The most important advantage of using this architecture is ‘the separation of concerns’. It separates the data, logic and the visual interface explicitly.  Other than that, it allows a more modular approach for developers; allowing them to work on multiple aspects of the web application at the same time without disturbing another. It also allows the flexibility for future enhancements as there is low coupling among models, views and controllers. It leaves more room for changes. For this project we have used PHP Laravel 5  MVC Framework as it provides a comprehensive boilerplate  which can be used as a foundation and built upon. It provides the BLADE Templating engine for the front end enabling amazing dynamic frontend UIs. It also includes a lot of pre -loaded powerful libr aries such as Carbon (for date time objects management), Guzzle (make HTTP requests) and a powerful Eloquent ORM (Object Relation Mapping) and a Query Builder which makes fetching and filtering data from the database much easier. Laravel also allows defining relationships between models e.g. assigning posts to users. This allows efficient model relation management and takes out the repetitiveness of joining tables again and again to find relevant data models. The architecture of Laravel also provides migrations which can acts as a ‘Version Control System’ for database structure.

heading: Abstract
content: The project is about developing an android application for providing assistance to the rescue organizations working in Pakistan. It would also provide quick menu for usability to complainants/victims with which the victims of an accident or the complainant (people reporting from the spot) can send rescue request which would be attended by an organization nearby (Rescue 1122 currently). The system that is currently being used by rescue is wireless system. Rescue teams communicate with hospitals through wireless system and rescue teams then communicat e to ambulance that is sent to place of disaster. The basic flaw in this system is that we do not have any real time monitoring of ambulance (We do not know exactly where the ambulance is). So such system is needed that can give real time monitoring of amb ulance. Recently applications are developed to rescue wild life in case of disaster. “IFAW Wildlife Rescue App” is an application that connects people to nearest rescue team or organization at the touch of a button to help native wildlife [1]. Similarly “EMNet findERnow” is an application that locates near hospital with respect to need of a patient [2]. The process of requesting and GUI of application would be simple for the complainants/victims and organizations. The rescue team can also install such appli cation on touchpad’s of vehicles, tables or smart phones through which they would be guided regarding location of the complainants/victim and hospitals near to them after attending complainants/victim.

content: Emotions are part of everyday life of a person. With day -to-day life, automatic emotion detection is becoming part of modern era computer science. Emotion detec tion can be used  in many applications such as crime interrogation, online interviews, and improving online gaming experiences. In addition to this, emotion reco gnition can also be used for educational purposes to perceive students' interest in a course and make it better so that students can understand well a nd much more. Most of the facial images are captured using normal digital cameras however, the main problem with the normal cameras is that they take a lot of effect from Illumination that eventually affects the picture being processed. Every single emotion affects your face with different amount of heat on your face and heat can easily be captured using therm al camera, which is helpful for emotion recognition even in bad Illumination conditions. This work used thermal ima gery for emotion recognition. We have used Histogram Oriented Gradient (HOG), a feature extraction technique to extract face features from th ermal images followed by Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier for recognition of different emotion types. With this  handcrafted technique, we achieved 70% accuracy on thermal infrared images and 75% on visual images using Natural visible and infrared facial expression database. Furthermore, to improve accuracy an experiment is done on deep neural network using transfer learning for feature extraction and classification as well. We achieve an accuracy about 90% on thermal infrared images and 95% on visual images. Afterwards, another experiment is done using hybrid approach that is transfer learning to extract features and passing these features to Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier for recognition of different emotions. We achieve an accuracy about 99.34% on thermal infrared images and 99.8% on visual images using a benchmark natural visible and infrared facial expression database.

heading: Objectives
content: In our project, we have focused on the implementation of emotion recognition from thermal human face image using image processing techniques.  The basic purpose of developing this project is to serve the society by identifying the criminals, prevent accidents on the road and to learn about the gamers experience in the gaming industry. Our system performs the following tasks:  Perform real time face detection while the user is interacting with it.  Development of reliable software for emotion recognition.  Maintaining database for thermal images.  Development of an optimized algorithm for emotion recognition based on existing images in the database.  Intelligent decision making on the basis of above-mentioned recognition technique.

content: The functional and non -functional requirements are introduced using the Unified Modelling Language (UML) which is an open method used to specify, visualize, construct and document the artefacts of an object -oriented software -intensive system under development. UML offers a standard way to write a system's blueprints, including conceptual components. Functional requirement defines a function of a software system or its component. A function is described as a set of inputs, the behaviour, and outputs. Functional requirements may be calculations, technical details, data manipulation and processing and other specific functionality that defines what a system is supposed to accomplish. Behavioural requirements describing all the cases where the system uses the functional requirements are captured in use cases. Non-functional requirement is a requirement that specifies criteria that can be used to judge the operation of a system, rather than specific behaviours. This should be contrasted with functional requirements that define specific behaviour or functions.

heading: Abstract
content: In this final year project, we have developed an automatic statistical machine translation system that  translates English language text to U rdu language and vice versa. As machine translation (or MT) becomes increasingly desired for more and more language pairs, these systems become a necessity. However, the current state -of-the-art research on English-Urdu statistical MT is quite bleak due to the unavailability of large-scale good quality parallel corpora. Such data is important for the development and evaluation of a reliable MT system. Therefore, one of the main contribution of this FYP work is the de velopment of a freely available and  large-scale parallel corpus for English-Urdu language pair. We have also performed statistical MT experiments using the Moses open source toolkit and report ed competitive evaluation results using  Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score. Table of Contents:

heading: Problem Statement
content: The main aim of this FYP is to build an English-Urdu SMT system.

heading: Objectives
content: Following are the goals and objectives of our FYP project. ▪ Explore the problem of SMT for English-Urdu language pair in detail. ▪ Develop a large-scale gold standard parallel corpus for English-Urdu language pair. ▪ Learn and use the open source SMT toolkit, Moses, for the development of English-Urdu SMT system. ▪ Effectively address the issues (e.g. word order) especially related to English-Urdu MT to improve the accuracy of the system. ▪ Perform evaluation of the developed system and report the Bi-Lingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score.

heading: Related Work
content: In this section, we have  describe the related work that has already been done  on English-Urdu SMT. In 2016 [2], the authors investigated different MT approaches for Indian languages including Urdu. The corpus used in experiments is EMILLE dataset [ 8]. There are 8,245 English -Urdu parallel sentences in the corpus which were divided into train and test set for training and evaluation. The relatively low BLEU score (0.14) reported after experiments was supported by the reason that the corpus is too small for realistic experiments and the sentences in the corpus are not properly aligned. In 2014 [ 9], the authors presented a baseline  for English -Urdu automatic MT system. They investigated phrase-base MT (PBMT) and hierarchical MT (HMT) for English -Urdu language pair. Their parallel corpus  was collected from AFRL (50,313 sentences), EMILLE (8 ,245 sentences) [8], IPC (7,478) [10], QURAN (6,364 sentences) and PENN (6,204 sentences) [11]. On all datasets, it was found that HMT (BLEU 21.35) performed better than PBMT (BLEU 18.30). However, the AFRL corpus used in the experiments is not publicly available. In another study [1 2], the authors highlighted the issues of development and sentence alignment of English-Urdu parallel corpus. The parallel corpus used was collected from Ahadeeths of Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. 7,275 Ahadeeths from Sahih Bukhari and 7,190 Ahadeeths from Sahih Muslim were used in this study. The authors used MOSES toolkit and BLEU  score reported was 8.39 before training and 9.03 after tuning. In 2013 [13], the authors evaluated Rule Based Machine Translation (RBMT), Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) and Example Based Machine Translation (EBMT) using a toy corpus of 7 parallel English-Urdu sentences. Moreover, for SMT evaluation, they used Google and Bing online

heading: Results
content: Data collected and prepared for experiment is 1,56,203 parallel sentences. Moses is used for training the English -Urdu automatic MT system. BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy Score) score is used to evaluate the results of the trained MT system. It is a score used for evaluating a machine translated sentence to the reference senten ce. A score of 1.0 indicates that it’s a perfect translation while a score of 0.0 shows a complete opposite. The whole corpus was used in the experiment, but it is divided into three sets. 75% of the data is used for training the system, 15% for tuning and 10% for testing.

heading: Abstract
content: Urdu language is a resource poor language when it comes to NLP research. Due to its highly rich morphological structure, it is hard to find basic NLP tools for the Urdu language . In this FYP project, w e developed a large  English-Urdu parallel corpus to train a Statistical Machine Translation System. We accomplished to collect and save a large  parallel corpus from different sources. The size of the dataset is 1,56,203 sentence pairs. The corpus is then preprocessed, cleaned and saved in standard format. We then performed  the experiment on Moses SMT toolkit to report the results. We have reported both before and after tuning results  on our parallel dataset, with a maximum value of 23.45 of BLEU score.

heading: Future Work
content: The low BLEU score of our system can be improved by using transliterations module to handle the OOV words problem. Furthermore, we also plan to increase the size and quality dataset.

heading: Introduction
content: Detection and monitoring of calories is trivial, not an easy task. It is very difficult to track daily calorie intake manually and not every person has knowledge about how many calories each food contains. People are facing health problems because of increase in weight and less exercise. By using calorie detector they can easily track their calories and can keep a proper chart of their meals. There are others scenarios in which we need calorie detector suc h as a people working in such companies or institutes where most of their time is spent sitting on the chair they have very less time for a workout and result in being overweight. So, if they want to keep track of their daily calories they can easily do th is and remain healthy. It can be used by someone conscious about their health and want to keep themselves fit.  And an old person who can’t do any exercise but wants to stay fit and healthy. Women are more conscious about their weight and they don’t have time for any kind of exercise especially for working women. it becomes very difficult for them to manage their work and health at the same time. So an application is required to solve above problems. The proposed system will tell the estimated calories by r ecognizing the food added by the registered user. Food can be entered manually and is saved in a specific category. Design and Development of calorie detector app to automatically recognize the food and tell its estimated calories. For this purpose, we have collected a dataset of six food categories i-e Burger, pizza, samosa, rolls, cupcake, and donuts and then train this dataset by using A.lexNet. This trained model will recognize the food by a picture and tell estimated calories and make a chart of daily calories intake by the user. The system will also make graphs of users weight and calories which will change according to their increase or decrease in weight or calories. The implementation of such a system will provide with a calorie detector which will help people to keep track of their daily consumption of calories and this system will automatically recognize the food the user just have to click a picture. It will also keep a record of daily, weekly and monthly meals and estimated calories.

heading: Introduction
content: Convolutional Neural Networks are just like the ordinary neural networks but they are made up of neurons that have learnable weights and biases. Each neuron receives some inputs, performs a dot product and optionally follows it with a non -linearity. The in puts to Convolution network are images, which allows us to encode certain properties into the architecture. Unlike the regular neural network which takes a single vector as input, the ConvNet takes an input in 3 dimensions such as width, height, and depth.  And transforms 3D input volume to 3D output volume of neurons activation.[8] The convolution neural network uses 4 main types of layers to build the architecture.  Convolution Layer: In this layer, we will take the Kernel/filter (piece of the image) and takes the dot product with the input image. The size of kernel and stride value will decide the output feature map size. And each filter is mapped on to each feature map. Such as if we have 10 filters then we have 10 feature maps  Pooling Layer: This layer will downsample the image. This layer is basically used to reduce the size. This layer is just after the convolution layer and takes convolution feature map as the input and prepare a condensed feature map. We have two types of pooling: L2-pooling, max-pooling. In max-pooling, we will take the maximum activation of the filter whereas in L2-pooling we will take the square root of the sum of the squares of the activations of the filter.  RELU Layer: RELU layer will apply the element-wise activation function and will update all the negative values of the feature map to zero. Such that the size of the volume remains unchanged.  Fully Connected Layer: FC layer will compute the class score just like the ordinary neural network. each neuron in this layer will be conne cted to all the neurons in the previous layer. This layer is basically used to predict the class label.
